Make the sprites with fal. 80 81 > Make a new civilization for Age of Empires II with a unique unit rendered from 3D. 82 83 > Put real Minecraft inside GTA V story mode. SkillWhat it does
mod-any-gameThe whole loop, hard safety rules, and engine playbooks: Unity, Unreal, .NET/XNA (Terraria, Stardew, Celeste), Godot, Source 1/2, Bethesda, Minecraft, AoE2/Genie, Bannerlord, Binding of Isaac, RE Engine/MT Framework/FromSoft/GTA/Hedgehog Engine/Black Rock/Cyberpunk/BG3/Avalanche, native C++, indie engines (GameMaker, RPG Maker, Ren'Py, Paradox, Doom, HTML5, LÖVE, Java), retro decomps
game-reconPrior field notes, engine and version, managed or native, anti-cheat, loaders, save folders, community route → MODDING_PLAN.md
game-research-websearchOpen-web research that survives dead forums: Wayback/archive.today, GitHub/code and Nexus/Workshop/Thunderstore APIs, Reddit/YouTube, login-gated handoff, screenshots as evidence
reverse-engineeringILSpy / Cpp2IL / Vineflower / Ghidra and IDA over MCP / Cheat Engine / Frida / RenderDoc; reverse-engineer a file format and prove it with a round trip
fal-assetsSprites with real transparency, consistent variants, pixel art, seamless textures, PBR maps, image-to-3D, auto-rigging, SFX, music, voice, cutscene video
asset-pipelineArt → engine-exact frames: cutout, nearest-neighbour fit, palettes, sheets, team-colour masks, 3D → 8/16-heading sprites

showcase-videoRecord the window with only the game's audio, pick moments, cut a styled video from an EDL

publish-modLint, package per platform, credits, the post
port-a-modPort an existing mod to a newer version or loader without drift: one pinned source, a private decompile, data extracted by script, unit-by-unit tests, audits by layer, resumable status docs, and a Forge 1.7.10 → Fabric 1.20.1 mapping table
share-field-notesSearch the knowledge base, write your own note, open the PR

Claude Code loads them with the plugin; in a clone, start with 153 `claude --plugin-dir . --agent mod-orchestrator`. Cursor plugins and Gemini CLI extensions read an `agents/` 154 folder too (untested here; Gemini CLI's subagents can't start other subagents). Three agents use several 155 times the tokens of one, so keep it for long mods. What worked for one user: the orchestrator on Fable 5.1 at 156 medium effort, the game worker on Sonnet 5.5 at medium, and the offline worker on Opus 5.5 at high. Any agent can 157 read the files as role briefs. 158 159 160 161 162 163 164 165 166
AgentWhat it does
mod-orchestratorThe supervisor. Plans the work, runs the two workers, checks what they claim against logs and files, and reports to the human in plain language. Start it as the main session: claude --agent mod-orchestrator
mod-game-workerThe only agent that touches the running game: build, deploy, launch, probe, measure, fix
mod-offline-workerNever touches the game: studies SDK data, dumps and other mods, designs features, writes generators and patches, tests them against stubs, and hands over the exact live probes to run
167 168 **The `um` CLI** (Python). Every command has `--help` with examples. 169 170 171 172 173 174 175 176 177 178 179 180 181 182 183 184 185 186 187 188 189 190
          CommandWhat it does
um scanFind Steam/Epic/Xbox installs; fingerprint engine and version, .NET vs native, anti-cheat, installed loaders, save folders, ranked routes
um falsprite, image, edit, rmbg, pixelate, upscale, texture, pbr, model3d, rig, sfx, music, voice, video, run, search, schema, price. Plain REST, with a manifest of every generation
um comfystatus, image (--sprite cuts it out), run (any workflow saved with Export (API)). Images from a local ComfyUI server, no API key
um sprixensprite (one style per project), animate (sprite id → one-row sheet), tile, projects, credits, key. 2D art from Sprixen's paid API, with a manifest of every generation
um voidlesssprite, rotate (8-way turns), animate (an animation set on one asset), presets, asset, fetch, credits, key. 2D art from Voidless's paid API, with a manifest of every generation
um spritecutout, fit, pixelate, palette, sheet, slice, frames, team-mask, seamless, preview
um render3dGLB → sprite frames from the game's camera (aoe2, iso8, trueiso, topdown, side, turntable) with Blender
um winshot, record (gfxcapture + process-loopback audio), drive (input that only reaches the game), ps, kill, launch, reg
um videocontact sheets, compile (EDL → titled, beat-cut video with music), mux, beats, first-frame
um backupSnapshot, diff and restore save folders
um publish checkBlocks shipping game files, decompiled code and leaked keys
um kbThe knowledge base: search, show, new, check, index, sync, pr
um fastfilelist, dump: the rawfiles (GSC, CSC, menus, tables) in your own Call of Duty 4 / World at War .ff zones. Read-only, unsigned PC zones
um iwipng2iwi (DXT1/DXT5, optional mip chain), iwi2png: Call of Duty 4 / World at War IWI v6 textures
um weaponget, set, clone, diff: Call of Duty 4 / World at War weapon files

=== AGENTS.md
# universal-modder

A game-modding toolkit and a shared knowledge base for AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini
CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode and anything else that reads `AGENTS.md`. When someone opens an agent in this
repo, they almost always want to **mod a game**, or to learn how a game was modded.

## Start here
1. **Read `skills/mod-any-game/SKILL.md` and follow its loop:** intake → recon → route → lab (backups) →
   source of truth → vertical slice → assets → verify in the real game → showcase → publish.
2. **Search the knowledge base first:** `bin/um kb search "<game or engine>"`. Other agents may already have
   written down the exact versions, routes and gotchas (`knowledge/INDEX.md`).
3. **At the end, share what you learned:** write a field note (`bin/um kb new ...`) and, once your human
   agrees, open a PR (`bin/um kb pr <note> --yes`). See `knowledge/README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Tools
- **`bin/um`** is the Python CLI, and it sets itself up with `uv`.
  - Put it on PATH: `export PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH"` (from Windows cmd or PowerShell, add `bin` to PATH and
    `bin\um.cmd` runs it), or install it anywhere with
    `uv tool install git+https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder`.
  - Every group has `--help`:
    - `scan`: installed games, engine, anti-cheat, loaders, saves, routes
    - `fal`: sprites, textures, PBR, 3D, rigs, SFX, music, voice, video via fal's REST API
    - `comfy`: images from a local ComfyUI server, with no API key
    - `sprixen`: 2D sprites, animation sheets and tiles via Sprixen's paid API (`SPRIXEN_API_KEY`)
    - `voidless`: 2D sprites, 8-way turns and animation sets via Voidless's paid API (`VOIDLESS_API_KEY`)
    - `sprite` / `render3d`: art → engine-ready frames (`render3d` needs Blender on PATH or `BLENDER=...`)
    - `win`: launch, screenshot, input, record on Windows (also from WSL)
    - `video`: contact sheets and EDL showcase edits
    - `backup`: snapshot and restore saves
    - `publish`: pre-release lint
    - `kb`: the knowledge base
    - `fastfile` / `iwi` / `weapon`: Call of Duty 4 and World at War: rawfiles out of your own `.ff` zones,
      PNG ↔ IWI textures, weapon-file edits
- **fal MCP server:** `https://mcp.fal.ai/mcp` with header `Authorization: Bearer $FAL_KEY`.
  - It's pre-configured per agent: `.mcp.json` (Claude Code), `.codex/config.toml` (Codex),
    `.cursor/mcp.json` (Cursor), `.vscode/mcp.json` (VS Code / Copilot), `gemini-extension.json`
    (Gemini CLI), `opencode.json` (OpenCode).
  - It needs `FAL_KEY` in the agent's environment; without it the server doesn't connect. fal's OAuth
    endpoint, `https://mcp.fal.ai/mcp-relay`, takes a browser sign-in instead (see `skills/fal-assets`).
  - No MCP? `um fal` does the same over REST. It also finds the key that `um fal key set` stored (the
    desktop keyring on Linux, `~/.secrets/fal-key` elsewhere).
- **Skills** (`skills/*/SKILL.md`, Agent Skills format) are copied where agents look for them in a clone:
  `.agents/skills` (Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode) and `.claude/skills` (Claude Code). Edit
  `skills/`, then copy it over; a test fails while the copies differ.
- **Engine playbooks:** `skills/mod-any-game/references/engines/`.
- **Worked examples:** `examples/terraria-tmodloader`, `examples/aoe2-de-civ`,
  `examples/minecraft-gta5-passthrough`, `examples/outer-wilds-portal-gun`, `examples/mindustry-homing`,
  `examples/cities-skylines-city-dashboard`.

## Rules (full reasoning in `skills/mod-any-game/references/safety.md`)
- **What you can mod:** any game the user owns: single-player, multiplayer, or servers the user hosts.
  - Never touch online clients protected by anti-cheat.
  - Never write cheats against other players (aimbots, ESP, speed hacks).
  - Never bypass anti-cheat, DRM or ownership checks.
- **Saves:** `um backup` saves before modded launches.
- **What you ship:** never commit or publish game files, extracted assets or decompiled code. Keep
  decompiles outside the repo.
- **Processes:** kill by exact PID (`um win kill`), never by name pattern.
- **Ask first** before:
  - driving the user's mouse and keyboard, and never focus a game with an online mode while they're typing;
  - installing loaders into game folders or changing the registry;
  - publishing anything, PRs included.
- **Keep a journal:** a `MODLOG.md` in the mod's working folder. It becomes your field note at the end.

## Working on the toolkit itself
- **Python:** 3.10+, deps Pillow, numpy and PyYAML (`uv` handles them via `bin/um`). Code lives in `um/`,
  one module per CLI group, each with `register(sub)` and a docstring that doubles as `--help`.
- **Windows tools:** `um/ps1/*.ps1` embed C# 5 (Windows PowerShell 5.1's compiler): no string
  interpolation, no `out var`, no expression-bodied members.
- **Tests:** `uv run --with pytest pytest -q tests`. CI also runs `um kb check --index` and
  `um publish check .`.
- **Wording:** keep skills and docs agent-neutral ("the agent", not a product name) except in sections
  about one specific agent.

=== SECURITY.md
# Security

## Reporting a vulnerability
Please report security problems privately, not in a public issue or pull request. Use **Report a
vulnerability** on the repository's **Security** tab (GitHub's private vulnerability reporting). If that button
isn't there, open an issue that asks for a private contact and leave the details out.

There are no release branches: fixes land on `main`.

## What's in scope
The code in this repository: the `um` CLI (`bin/um`, `um/`, the PowerShell tools in `um/ps1/`), the hooks, the
agent configs and the example mods. The parts where a bug matters most:
- **Secrets.** `um fal` reads `FAL_KEY` from the environment, the key `um fal key set` stored (the desktop
  keyring on Linux, `~/.secrets/fal-key` elsewhere) or a `.env` file, and the agent configs pass `FAL_KEY` to
  the fal MCP server. A way for `um` to leak it, or a common key format that `um kb check` and
  `um publish check` miss, is in scope.
- **Local input and processes.** `um win` drives real input on Windows and kills processes by PID. Input that
  reaches a window other than the target game, or a kill that hits the wrong process, is in scope.
- **The Minecraft x GTA V example's link** listens on `127.0.0.1:25599` without a token, by design (see its
  README). A way to reach it from another machine is in scope.

Out of scope: problems in the tools and services `um` calls or downloads (fal, ComfyUI, ffmpeg, Blender, mod
loaders, ReShade, ScriptHookV). Please report those upstream. Requests to get past a game's anti-cheat, DRM or
ownership checks are out of scope too: this project doesn't do that (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

   written down the exact versions, routes and gotchas (`knowledge/INDEX.md`).
3. **At the end, share what you learned:** write a field note (`bin/um kb new ...`) and, once your human
   agrees, open a PR (`bin/um kb pr <note> --yes`). See `knowledge/README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Tools
- **`bin/um`** is the Python CLI, and it sets itself up with `uv`.
  - Put it on PATH: `export PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH"` (from Windows cmd or PowerShell, add `bin` to PATH and
    `bin\um.cmd` runs it), or install it anywhere with
    `uv tool install git+https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder`.
  - Every group has `--help`:
    - `scan`: installed games, engine, anti-cheat, loaders, saves, routes
    - `fal`: sprites, textures, PBR, 3D, rigs, SFX, music, voice, video via fal's REST API
    - `comfy`: images from a local ComfyUI server, with no API key
    - `sprixen`: 2D sprites, animation sheets and tiles via Sprixen's paid API (`SPRIXEN_API_KEY`)
    - `voidless`: 2D sprites, 8-way turns and animation sets via Voidless's paid API (`VOIDLESS_API_KEY`)
    - `sprite` / `render3d`: art → engine-ready frames (`render3d` needs Blender on PATH or `BLENDER=...`)
    - `win`: launch, screenshot, input, record on Windows (also from WSL)
    - `video`: contact sheets and EDL showcase edits
    - `backup`: snapshot and restore saves
    - `publish`: pre-release lint
    - `kb`: the knowledge base
    - `fastfile` / `iwi` / `weapon`: Call of Duty 4 and World at War: rawfiles out of your own `.ff` zones,
      PNG ↔ IWI textures, weapon-file edits
- **fal MCP server:** `https://mcp.fal.ai/mcp` with header `Authorization: Bearer $FAL_KEY`.
  - It's pre-configured per agent: `.mcp.json` (Claude Code), `.codex/config.toml` (Codex),
    `.cursor/mcp.json` (Cursor), `.vscode/mcp.json` (VS Code / Copilot), `gemini-extension.json`
    (Gemini CLI), `opencode.json` (OpenCode).
  - It needs `FAL_KEY` in the agent's environment; without it the server doesn't connect. fal's OAuth
    endpoint, `https://mcp.fal.ai/mcp-relay`, takes a browser sign-in instead (see `skills/fal-assets`).
  - No MCP? `um fal` does the same over REST. It also finds the key that `um fal key set` stored (the
    desktop keyring on Linux, `~/.secrets/fal-key` elsewhere).
- **Skills** (`skills/*/SKILL.md`, Agent Skills format) are copied where agents look for them in a clone:
  `.agents/skills` (Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode) and `.claude/skills` (Claude Code). Edit
  `skills/`, then copy it over; a test fails while the copies differ.
- **Engine playbooks:** `skills/mod-any-game/references/engines/`.
- **Worked examples:** `examples/terraria-tmodloader`, `examples/aoe2-de-civ`,
  `examples/minecraft-gta5-passthrough`, `examples/outer-wilds-portal-gun`, `examples/mindustry-homing`,
  `examples/cities-skylines-city-dashboard`.

## Rules (full reasoning in `skills/mod-any-game/references/safety.md`)
- **What you can mod:** any game the user owns: single-player, multiplayer, or servers the user hosts.
  - Never touch online clients protected by anti-cheat.
  - Never write cheats against other players (aimbots, ESP, speed hacks).
  - Never bypass anti-cheat, DRM or ownership checks.
- **Saves:** `um backup` saves before modded launches.
- **What you ship:** never commit or publish game files, extracted assets or decompiled code. Keep
  decompiles outside the repo.
- **Processes:** kill by exact PID (`um win kill`), never by name pattern.
- **Ask first** before:
  - driving the user's mouse and keyboard, and never focus a game with an online mode while they're typing;
  - installing loaders into game folders or changing the registry;
  - publishing anything, PRs included.
- **Keep a journal:** a `MODLOG.md` in the mod's working folder. It becomes your field note at the end.

## Working on the toolkit itself
- **Python:** 3.10+, deps Pillow, numpy and PyYAML (`uv` handles them via `bin/um`). Code lives in `um/`,
  one module per CLI group, each with `register(sub)` and a docstring that doubles as `--help`.
- **Windows tools:** `um/ps1/*.ps1` embed C# 5 (Windows PowerShell 5.1's compiler): no string
  interpolation, no `out var`, no expression-bodied members.
- **Tests:** `uv run --with pytest pytest -q tests`. CI also runs `um kb check --index` and
  `um publish check .`.
- **Wording:** keep skills and docs agent-neutral ("the agent", not a product name) except in sections
  about one specific agent.

=== SECURITY.md
# Security

## Reporting a vulnerability
Please report security problems privately, not in a public issue or pull request. Use **Report a
vulnerability** on the repository's **Security** tab (GitHub's private vulnerability reporting). If that button
isn't there, open an issue that asks for a private contact and leave the details out.

There are no release branches: fixes land on `main`.

## What's in scope
The code in this repository: the `um` CLI (`bin/um`, `um/`, the PowerShell tools in `um/ps1/`), the hooks, the
agent configs and the example mods. The parts where a bug matters most:
- **Secrets.** `um fal` reads `FAL_KEY` from the environment, the key `um fal key set` stored (the desktop
  keyring on Linux, `~/.secrets/fal-key` elsewhere) or a `.env` file, and the agent configs pass `FAL_KEY` to
  the fal MCP server. A way for `um` to leak it, or a common key format that `um kb check` and
  `um publish check` miss, is in scope.
- **Local input and processes.** `um win` drives real input on Windows and kills processes by PID. Input that
  reaches a window other than the target game, or a kill that hits the wrong process, is in scope.
- **The Minecraft x GTA V example's link** listens on `127.0.0.1:25599` without a token, by design (see its
  README). A way to reach it from another machine is in scope.

Out of scope: problems in the tools and services `um` calls or downloads (fal, ComfyUI, ffmpeg, Blender, mod
loaders, ReShade, ScriptHookV). Please report those upstream. Requests to get past a game's anti-cheat, DRM or
ownership checks are out of scope too: this project doesn't do that (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

1	# Minecraft
2	
3	## Java Edition: code mods with Fabric (or NeoForge)
4	- **Fabric:** a light loader and Fabric API, with Mixin for bytecode patches. It updates fast to new
5	  versions.
6	  1. Get the template from https://fabricmc.net/develop/template/, or clone `FabricMC/fabric-example-mod`.
7	  2. Build with `./gradlew build`. The jar goes to `mods/`. `./gradlew runClient` launches a dev client with
8	     your mod (the perfect agent oracle: logs in `run/logs/latest.log`).
9	- **NeoForge:** the successor of Forge for modern versions (MDK template), with a bigger API surface
10	  (capabilities, events).
11	- **Forge (1.20.1, 47.x):** still the loader of many CurseForge instances. MDK with official mappings,
12	  JDK 17. `./gradlew runServer` / `runClient` are the oracles; gate any self-test behind a Gradle
13	  property (e.g. `-Pselftest`) so it is inert in a real world. Never run two Gradle builds at once.
14	- **Mappings:** Mojang publishes official obfuscation maps. Loom (Fabric) handles Yarn or Mojang mappings
15	  and produces readable sources: `./gradlew genSources`.
16	- **Content:** register items, blocks, entities and sounds through the registries. Assets go under
17	  `src/main/resources/assets/<modid>/` (textures 16x16 PNG, models JSON, lang JSON, sounds.json + ogg).
18	  Data (recipes, loot tables, tags) goes under `data/<modid>/`.
19	- **Server-side only:** plugins (Paper/Spigot) plus resource packs change a lot without client mods. The
20	  "Black Ops 2 inside vanilla Minecraft" demo was a plugin plus a resource pack.
21	- `minecraft-modding-mcp` gives an agent mappings, decompiled source and version diffs.
22	
23	## Porting an old Forge mod (1.7.10 / 1.12) to modern Fabric
24	- Use the **port-a-mod** skill. It covers the original's license (which decides whether the port can be
25	  published) and the method: one pinned source version, a private remapped decompile, an adaptation matrix,
26	  data extracted by scripts, unit-by-unit GameTests, audits by layer, and resumable status docs.
27	- Its `references/minecraft-1-7-10-forge-to-1-20-fabric.md` maps Forge 1.7.10 concepts to Fabric 1.20.1. For
28	  example:
29	  - `onItemUseFirst` → `UseBlockCallback`;
30	  - metadata → flattened ids;
31	  - ISBRH → FRAPI;
32	  - `IItemRenderer` → builtin item renderers;
33	  - Baubles → Accessories;
34	  - DamageSource flags → damage-type tags.
35	- **Decompile and remap:** 1.7.10 jars use SRG names. Use Vineflower, CFR for the classes it fails on, and the
36	  MCP `stable_12` CSVs. Read the target's mapped jar with `javap` from the Loom cache.
37	- **Oracles:**
38	  - GameTests on the real test server:
39	    `knowledge/techniques/fabric-1-20-1-gametests-as-the-oracle-of-a-large-mod-port.md`;
40	  - a scripted real client:
41	    `knowledge/techniques/a-scenario-harness-in-a-minecraft-fabric-dev-client-real-cli.md`;
42	  - the release jar on a real server.
43	- **Rendering:** 1.7.10 GL11 states (alpha test, `GL_ADD`, brightness, `IItemRenderer` frames, `ModelBox`
44	  mirroring) are mapped in
45	  `knowledge/techniques/porting-1-7-10-gl11-render-states-and-iitemrenderer-frames-t.md`.
46	- **Worked example:** Thaumcraft 4.2.3.5 → 1.20.1 Fabric (323 GameTests). See
47	  `knowledge/games/minecraft/porting-thaumcraft-4-1-7-10-forge-to-minecraft-1-20-1-fabric.md`.
48	- **Cloud and sandboxed builds:** Loom needs `maven.fabricmc.net` and Mojang's `piston-meta`, `piston-data`,
49	  `libraries.minecraft.net` and `resources.download.minecraft.net`. A populated Loom cache builds offline. The
50	  test server's "Cannot contact authentication server" line is harmless.
51	
52	## Bedrock Edition: add-ons
53	Behavior packs (JSON entities/items/blocks + Script API in JavaScript/TypeScript, `@minecraft/server`) and
54	resource packs. Develop in `com.mojang/development_*_packs` and turn on content-log output for errors.
55	
56	## Pitfalls
57	- Match the exact game version + loader version + API version triple; mods are version-locked.
58	- **Minecraft 26.3 facts from the GTA passthrough project** (`knowledge/games/gta-v/minecraft-passthrough.md`):
59	  - A depth readback (`copyTextureToBuffer`) leaves the read buffer at `GL_NONE`, so later colour readbacks
60	    fail. Restore it in a mixin.
61	  - Fabric's `JOIN` event fires before the player is in the player list; delay setup commands by ~10 ticks.
62	  - An entity's Invisible flag resets on first sync unless it has an effect.
63	  - Invulnerable entities can't be targeted by mobs.
64	  - With `noPhysics`, `onGround` sticks, so elytra glides get cancelled.
65	- **Forge 1.20.1 facts from the Bloons TD 6 mashup** (`knowledge/games/minecraft/bloons-td-6-in-minecraft.md`):
66	  - Writing the TOML at runtime with `ConfigValue.set()` + `save()` can truncate it: the file is written
67	    in place while Forge's watcher (night-config 3.6.4) re-reads it. Keep the live value in memory and
68	    write a sibling temp file, then rename it over the original.
69	  - That watcher also misses many editor saves (it ignores aggregated modify events): poll the mtime.
70	  - Forge never rewrites a value already in the TOML, so a changed default never reaches existing users.
71	    Write floats as `1.0`, not `1`.
72	  - Buckets bypass `EntityPlaceEvent` (Forge does not capture their placement). To police fluids, listen
73	    to `NeighborNotifyEvent` and act in the same tick.
74	  - Any `MOVEMENT_SPEED` modifier widens the FOV; undo only your term in `ComputeFovModifierEvent`.
75	  - Chunks rebuilt server-side can stay invisible until the camera changes section (the client's
76	    visible-section graph is cached): call `LevelRenderer.needsUpdate()` a few seconds later.
77	  - Minecraft only attenuates and positions **mono** sounds; convert stereo sources to mono.
78	  - Dev runs use Mojang names, the shipped jar SRG names: anything matching methods by name passes the
79	    benches and fails in the real game. Have the human run the real jar in the real instance.
80	  - Give the network channel an explicit protocol version so a client with another jar is refused at
81	    login instead of crashing mid-game.
82	- **Fabric 1.20.1 facts from the Thaumcraft 4 port**
83	  (`knowledge/games/minecraft/porting-thaumcraft-4-1-7-10-forge-to-minecraft-1-20-1-fabric.md`):
84	  - The GameTest server has no datapack dimensions. Test dimension content in the overworld.
85	  - A flat generator whose layers are all air runs no features. Add one `structure_void` layer.
86	  - A datapack dimension marks worlds experimental through two checks; both are patched by one mixin.
87	  - `World.getBiome(pos)` is blended by seed. Read the stored cell with `getBiomeForNoiseGen` to match what
88	    you wrote.
89	  - 1.7.10 world generators wrote into neighbouring chunks, but 1.20 features may not. Split the writes, and
90	    shift ported `decorate(x, z)` frames by -8.
91	  - A Fabric `FakePlayer` is invulnerable. `createMockCreativeServerPlayerInWorld` leaks into the whole test
92	    batch.
93	  - Mod jars built with a newer Loom refuse to remap. Raise Loom (1.6 → 1.7.4 worked).
94	  - cloth-config's pom drags an old loader onto the classpath. Declare it `transitive = false`.
95	  - The Accessories Trinkets layer `provides` trinkets, so Fabric Loader silently drops real Trinkets.
96	- **A separate launcher profile keeps the user's worlds safe.** Add a Fabric profile with its own `gameDir`.
97	  `fabric-installer -launcher microsoft_store` fails for lack of `launcher_profiles_microsoft_store.json`,
98	  so edit `launcher_profiles.json` by hand, after a backup.
99	- Multiplayer: a server needs the mod too (or use plugins). Never ship client hacks for public servers.
100	- **Port fidelity:**
101	  - A 1.7.10 `Item.onItemUseFirst` ran before the block's `onBlockActivated`. In 1.20 the block's `onUse` runs
102	    first, so items that must win go through `UseBlockCallback`.
103	  - Many 1.7.10 mods checked on the client first and showed a chat message before asking the server. Port that
104	    pre-check too, or the port refuses silently.
105	- Mashups: the September 2026 "Minecraft inside X" projects either reimplemented Minecraft (Rust rewrites
106	  matching Java worldgen) or ran it side by side and exchanged state (passthrough). Minecraft's own assets
107	  were downloaded from Mojang at first run and never redistributed.

- **Rendering:** 1.7.10 GL11 states (alpha test, `GL_ADD`, brightness, `IItemRenderer` frames, `ModelBox`
  mirroring) are mapped in
  `knowledge/techniques/porting-1-7-10-gl11-render-states-and-iitemrenderer-frames-t.md`.
- **Worked example:** Thaumcraft 4.2.3.5 → 1.20.1 Fabric (323 GameTests). See
  `knowledge/games/minecraft/porting-thaumcraft-4-1-7-10-forge-to-minecraft-1-20-1-fabric.md`.
- **Cloud and sandboxed builds:** Loom needs `maven.fabricmc.net` and Mojang's `piston-meta`, `piston-data`,
  `libraries.minecraft.net` and `resources.download.minecraft.net`. A populated Loom cache builds offline. The
  test server's "Cannot contact authentication server" line is harmless.

## Bedrock Edition: add-ons
Behavior packs (JSON entities/items/blocks + Script API in JavaScript/TypeScript, `@minecraft/server`) and
resource packs. Develop in `com.mojang/development_*_packs` and turn on content-log output for errors.

## Pitfalls
- Match the exact game version + loader version + API version triple; mods are version-locked.
- **Minecraft 26.3 facts from the GTA passthrough project** (`knowledge/games/gta-v/minecraft-passthrough.md`):
  - A depth readback (`copyTextureToBuffer`) leaves the read buffer at `GL_NONE`, so later colour readbacks
    fail. Restore it in a mixin.
  - Fabric's `JOIN` event fires before the player is in the player list; delay setup commands by ~10 ticks.
  - An entity's Invisible flag resets on first sync unless it has an effect.
  - Invulnerable entities can't be targeted by mobs.
  - With `noPhysics`, `onGround` sticks, so elytra glides get cancelled.
- **Forge 1.20.1 facts from the Bloons TD 6 mashup** (`knowledge/games/minecraft/bloons-td-6-in-minecraft.md`):
  - Writing the TOML at runtime with `ConfigValue.set()` + `save()` can truncate it: the file is written
    in place while Forge's watcher (night-config 3.6.4) re-reads it. Keep the live value in memory and
    write a sibling temp file, then rename it over the original.
  - That watcher also misses many editor saves (it ignores aggregated modify events): poll the mtime.
  - Forge never rewrites a value already in the TOML, so a changed default never reaches existing users.
    Write floats as `1.0`, not `1`.
  - Buckets bypass `EntityPlaceEvent` (Forge does not capture their placement). To police fluids, listen
    to `NeighborNotifyEvent` and act in the same tick.
  - Any `MOVEMENT_SPEED` modifier widens the FOV; undo only your term in `ComputeFovModifierEvent`.
  - Chunks rebuilt server-side can stay invisible until the camera changes section (the client's
    visible-section graph is cached): call `LevelRenderer.needsUpdate()` a few seconds later.
  - Minecraft only attenuates and positions **mono** sounds; convert stereo sources to mono.
  - Dev runs use Mojang names, the shipped jar SRG names: anything matching methods by name passes the
    benches and fails in the real game. Have the human run the real jar in the real instance.
  - Give the network channel an explicit protocol version so a client with another jar is refused at
    login instead of crashing mid-game.
- **Fabric 1.20.1 facts from the Thaumcraft 4 port**
  (`knowledge/games/minecraft/porting-thaumcraft-4-1-7-10-forge-to-minecraft-1-20-1-fabric.md`):
  - The GameTest server has no datapack dimensions. Test dimension content in the overworld.
  - A flat generator whose layers are all air runs no features. Add one `structure_void` layer.
  - A datapack dimension marks worlds experimental through two checks; both are patched by one mixin.
  - `World.getBiome(pos)` is blended by seed. Read the stored cell with `getBiomeForNoiseGen` to match what
    you wrote.
  - 1.7.10 world generators wrote into neighbouring chunks, but 1.20 features may not. Split the writes, and
    shift ported `decorate(x, z)` frames by -8.
  - A Fabric `FakePlayer` is invulnerable. `createMockCreativeServerPlayerInWorld` leaks into the whole test
    batch.
  - Mod jars built with a newer Loom refuse to remap. Raise Loom (1.6 → 1.7.4 worked).
  - cloth-config's pom drags an old loader onto the classpath. Declare it `transitive = false`.
  - The Accessories Trinkets layer `provides` trinkets, so Fabric Loader silently drops real Trinkets.
- **A separate launcher profile keeps the user's worlds safe.** Add a Fabric profile with its own `gameDir`.
  `fabric-installer -launcher microsoft_store` fails for lack of `launcher_profiles_microsoft_store.json`,
  so edit `launcher_profiles.json` by hand, after a backup.
- Multiplayer: a server needs the mod too (or use plugins). Never ship client hacks for public servers.
- **Port fidelity:**
  - A 1.7.10 `Item.onItemUseFirst` ran before the block's `onBlockActivated`. In 1.20 the block's `onUse` runs
    first, so items that must win go through `UseBlockCallback`.
  - Many 1.7.10 mods checked on the client first and showed a chat message before asking the server. Port that
    pre-check too, or the port refuses silently.
- Mashups: the September 2026 "Minecraft inside X" projects either reimplemented Minecraft (Rust rewrites
  matching Java worldgen) or ran it side by side and exchanged state (passthrough). Minecraft's own assets
  were downloaded from Mojang at first run and never redistributed.

40	
41	## The loop
42	
43	### 0. Intake (keep it short)
44	- Get the game, the platform and store, and the idea in one sentence ("a homing missile launcher and a nuke
45	  that craters the world"). Also agree what done means; usually that's working in game plus a 20-45 s clip.
46	- If the user wants an existing mod updated to a newer game version or another loader (an old Forge 1.7.10
47	  mod on modern Fabric, say), the original is the spec, and its license decides whether the port can be
48	  published: follow the **port-a-mod** skill inside this loop.
49	- Settle online vs offline up front. If the game is online or competitive and has anti-cheat, don't mod the
50	  client (see Hard rules). Offer offline modes, private servers the user runs, or the official tools
51	  (Workshop, creative/map editors).
52	- Start `MODLOG.md` in the working folder as the journal. Record paths, IDs, file formats, class names, what
53	  failed and why, and the next step. Anything not in the journal is lost at the next context compaction.
54	
55	### 1. Recon (the game-recon skill does this in depth)
56	- **Search the knowledge base first.** Run `um kb search "<game>"` and `um kb search "<engine>"`. If
57	  another agent left a field note, start from its exact versions, route and gotchas, and don't repeat its
58	  dead ends. Without `um`, read
59	  https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder/blob/main/knowledge/INDEX.md.
60	- Run `um scan "<game>"`. It reports this machine's OS and CPU (`host:`), the engine and version, whether code
61	  is managed or native, anti-cheat, mod loaders already installed, save folders, ranked routes, and which
62	  playbook in `references/engines/` to read. Read that playbook.
63	- Research the community as it is now: the wiki's modding page, Nexus / Thunderstore / mod.io / Workshop,
64	  GitHub, and the loader's current release and install steps. Versions move, so don't install from memory.
65	  If the community already has a loader (tModLoader, SMAPI, BepInEx, UE4SS, REFramework, SKSE, Fabric),
66	  use it.
67	
68	### 2. Pick the cheapest route that reaches the idea
69	
70	| Route | When | Examples |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| Data / assets only | the idea fits the game's data files | AoE2 `.dat` via genieutils, Bethesda ESP/ESL, Paradox scripts, JSON content packs, pak overrides |
73	| Loader API | a loader exposes hooks for it | tModLoader `ModItem`/`ModNPC`, SMAPI, BepInEx plugin, UE4SS Lua, REFramework Lua, SKSE plugin |
74	| Managed-code patching | .NET/Mono/IL2CPP/Java with no API for your idea | Harmony prefix/postfix/transpiler, MonoMod, Mixin |
75	| Native hooks | C/C++ engine with no loader | proxy DLL (`dinput8`/`version`/`winmm`) + MinHook/SafetyHook, signature scans |
76	| Reimplement / decomp / recomp | total control, or retro consoles | N64 decomps, N64Recomp, XenonRecomp, IW4L-style rewrites that read the user's own game files |
77	| Mashup / passthrough | two games at once | the **mashup-mods** skill |
78	
79	Write the chosen route and the reason into MODLOG.md before building.
80	
81	### 3. Lab setup (the safety net)
82	- Before the first modded launch, run `um backup create "<saves folder>" --name <game>-saves` (the paths come
83	  from `um scan`). Snapshot the config/profile folder too if you'll change settings.
84	- Use a separate lab profile or save folder when the loader allows it (tModLoader
85	  `-tmlsavedirectory`, an MO2 profile, a copy of the world or scenario). Scripted takes destroy test worlds,
86	  so keep a pristine copy and restore it before every take.
87	- Use windowed mode at a known client size (registry/ini, see game-automation) so screenshots and click
88	  coordinates stay stable.
89	- Keep decompiled code and extracted assets outside the repo (e.g. `~/<game>-decomp`) and gitignore any
90	  derived data. Never commit game files.
91	
92	### 4. Read the source of truth
93	Read the actual code and data instead of guessing how the engine behaves. The **reverse-engineering** skill
94	covers the tools:
95	- decompile: ILSpy/`ilspycmd`, Cpp2IL, Vineflower, Ghidra/IDA over MCP;
96	- dump data: genieutils, xEdit, UndertaleModTool, FModel;
97	- inspect live: UnityExplorer, the UE4SS live viewer, REFramework, Cheat Engine.
98	
99	Record exact names and IDs in MODLOG.md. Check what the executable enforces as well as what the data says.
100	In AoE2 the data happily holds a 64th civilization, but the civ picker only lists civs from a table
101	hard-coded in the exe, so the mod replaces a slot instead of adding one.
102	
103	### 5. Vertical slice first
104	Take one item, unit or weapon all the way through with placeholder art. Define it, launch, and prove it
105	appears and works, from the log plus a screenshot you actually look at. Only then widen. Commit each working
106	step in the mod's own git repo.
107	
108	### 6. Assets (fal-assets and asset-pipeline skills)
109	Study the game's own assets first: size, palette, outline, camera angle, facing, frame layout. Then generate
110	with `um fal`. Every call is recorded in `fal_manifest.jsonl`. Convert with `um sprite` / `um render3d` into
111	exactly what the engine loads.
112	- **Consistency across many angles and frames:** generate one concept, turn it into 3D
113	  (`um fal model3d`), then render every heading from the game's camera (`um render3d --preset aoe2`).
114	- **Pixel-art games:** generate on a flat background or with transparency, cut out, then do one
115	  nearest-neighbour fit to the frame size.
116	
117	### 7. Verify in the real game (build an oracle)
118	The running game is the oracle; your reading of the code is not.
119	- Make the test repeatable: a mod-side chat command or timeline, a scenario with triggers, or a test world.
120	  Drive the launch → menus → scene path with `um win launch/drive`, and check it with `um win shot` plus the
121	  game's log files.
122	- Read screenshots at reduced scale (`--scale 0.33`) to save tokens; multiply coordinates back when clicking.
123	- **Circuit breaker:** if the same failure repeats 3 times, stop. Write down what you know, then change
124	  approach or ask the user.
125	- Common log locations:
126	
127	| Game / loader | Log |
128	|---|---|
129	| tModLoader | `client.log` |
130	| BepInEx | `BepInEx/LogOutput.log` |
131	| UE4SS | `UE4SS.log` |
132	| Unity | `Player.log` in `AppData/LocalLow/<company>/<product>/` |
133	| SKSE | `Documents/My Games/<game>/SKSE/` |
134	| Minecraft | `logs/latest.log` |
135	
136	### 8. Showcase (the showcase-video skill)
137	Script the take so it's repeatable. Record the game window with the game's own audio (`um win record`).
138	Choose moments from a contact sheet, then cut 20-45 s with one-line titles and a fade-out
139	(`um video compile`).
140	
141	### 9. Package and publish (the publish-mod skill)
142	Run `um publish check <mod> --game "<install>"`. Write a README with install steps. Credit tools, loaders and
143	fal-generated assets, and be honest that it was built with AI. Ship no game files.
144	
145	### 10. Leave a field note (the share-field-notes skill)
146	Turn `MODLOG.md` into a knowledge-base note (`um kb new ...`, then `um kb check`). Cover:
147	- exact versions;
148	- the route;
149	- what the engine really does;
150	- how you verified it;
151	- numbered gotchas.
152	
153	With your human's OK, open a PR (`um kb pr <note> --yes`). Do this even if the mod isn't finished: a
154	documented dead end saves the next agent hours.
155	
156	## Hard rules
157	- **Ownership.** Only mod games the user owns.
158	- **Online play.** Stay in single-player/offline, or on servers the user controls. Never touch the client of
159	  an online game protected by anti-cheat (EasyAntiCheat, BattlEye, Vanguard, VAC on official servers,
160	  Ricochet, ACE). Never write cheats (aimbots, ESP, speedhacks) for multiplayer.
161	- **No bypasses.** Never bypass anti-cheat, DRM or ownership checks. tModLoader refuses to start unless the
162	  free tModLoader app is in the user's Steam library: add it, don't patch the check. If a game needs its
163	  anti-cheat off for mods, use only the official offline launch option.
164	- **No redistribution.** Don't ship game files, decompiled source or extracted assets. Ship your own code and
165	  assets, or patches and converters that run on the user's own install ("bring your own game files").
166	- **Back up first.** Run `um backup` before changing saves, profiles or game folders. Keep the restore path
167	  written in MODLOG.md.
168	- **Process hygiene.**
169	  - Kill by exact PID (`um win kill <pid>`). Never use `pkill -f` (it matches your own shell) or wildcard
170	    kills.
171	  - Never block the game's main thread (for example by waiting on ffmpeg from inside a mod).
172	  - Clear crash reporters (BugSplat etc.) by PID when Steam refuses to relaunch.
173	- **The user's machine.**
174	  - Driving input takes over their mouse and keyboard. Check `um win drive --proc X idle` and ask before long
175	    automated sessions while they're at the PC.
176	  - Ask before installing a loader into the game folder, changing registry or graphics settings, deleting
177	    anything, or publishing.
178	
179	## References
180	- `references/engines/`:
181	  - big engines: `unity.md`, `unreal.md`, `godot.md`, `source.md`, `native.md`;
182	  - families and frameworks: `dotnet-xna.md` (Terraria, Stardew, Celeste), `bethesda.md`,
183	    `iw-engine.md` (Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare and World at War: IW 3.0/T4),
184	    `big-frameworks.md` (RE Engine, MT Framework, FromSoft, GTA, Hedgehog Engine, Black Rock, Cyberpunk,
185	    BG3, Avalanche/Just Cause), `misc-engines.md` (GameMaker, RPG Maker, Ren'Py, Paradox, Doom, HTML5, LÖVE,
186	    Java, Dwarf Fortress), `zengin.md` (Gothic 1/2: Daedalus scripts, Union, GD3D11);
187	  - single games and retro: `bannerlord.md` (Mount & Blade II: modules, XML/XSLT, C# SubModules, Harmony),
188	    `minecraft.md`, `genie-aoe2.md`, `isaac.md` (Binding of Isaac: Lua mods, REPENTOGON, anm2, console),
189	    `retro-decomp.md`.
190	- `references/case-studies.md`: Terraria, AoE2 and Minecraft × GTA V end to end, every non-obvious fact.
191	- The knowledge base (`knowledge/` at the repo root; `um kb search`): field notes by many agents, per game
192	  and per technique.
193	- `references/safety.md`: the rules with their reasons, anti-cheat and legal hygiene.

The running game is the oracle; your reading of the code is not.
- Make the test repeatable: a mod-side chat command or timeline, a scenario with triggers, or a test world.
  Drive the launch → menus → scene path with `um win launch/drive`, and check it with `um win shot` plus the
  game's log files.
- Read screenshots at reduced scale (`--scale 0.33`) to save tokens; multiply coordinates back when clicking.
- **Circuit breaker:** if the same failure repeats 3 times, stop. Write down what you know, then change
  approach or ask the user.
- Common log locations:

| Game / loader | Log |
|---|---|
| tModLoader | `client.log` |
| BepInEx | `BepInEx/LogOutput.log` |
| UE4SS | `UE4SS.log` |
| Unity | `Player.log` in `AppData/LocalLow/<company>/<product>/` |
| SKSE | `Documents/My Games/<game>/SKSE/` |
| Minecraft | `logs/latest.log` |

### 8. Showcase (the showcase-video skill)
Script the take so it's repeatable. Record the game window with the game's own audio (`um win record`).
Choose moments from a contact sheet, then cut 20-45 s with one-line titles and a fade-out
(`um video compile`).

### 9. Package and publish (the publish-mod skill)
Run `um publish check <mod> --game "<install>"`. Write a README with install steps. Credit tools, loaders and
fal-generated assets, and be honest that it was built with AI. Ship no game files.

### 10. Leave a field note (the share-field-notes skill)
Turn `MODLOG.md` into a knowledge-base note (`um kb new ...`, then `um kb check`). Cover:
- exact versions;
- the route;
- what the engine really does;
- how you verified it;
- numbered gotchas.

With your human's OK, open a PR (`um kb pr <note> --yes`). Do this even if the mod isn't finished: a
documented dead end saves the next agent hours.

## Hard rules
- **Ownership.** Only mod games the user owns.
- **Online play.** Stay in single-player/offline, or on servers the user controls. Never touch the client of
  an online game protected by anti-cheat (EasyAntiCheat, BattlEye, Vanguard, VAC on official servers,
  Ricochet, ACE). Never write cheats (aimbots, ESP, speedhacks) for multiplayer.
- **No bypasses.** Never bypass anti-cheat, DRM or ownership checks. tModLoader refuses to start unless the
  free tModLoader app is in the user's Steam library: add it, don't patch the check. If a game needs its
  anti-cheat off for mods, use only the official offline launch option.
- **No redistribution.** Don't ship game files, decompiled source or extracted assets. Ship your own code and
  assets, or patches and converters that run on the user's own install ("bring your own game files").
- **Back up first.** Run `um backup` before changing saves, profiles or game folders. Keep the restore path
  written in MODLOG.md.
- **Process hygiene.**
  - Kill by exact PID (`um win kill <pid>`). Never use `pkill -f` (it matches your own shell) or wildcard
    kills.
  - Never block the game's main thread (for example by waiting on ffmpeg from inside a mod).
  - Clear crash reporters (BugSplat etc.) by PID when Steam refuses to relaunch.
- **The user's machine.**
  - Driving input takes over their mouse and keyboard. Check `um win drive --proc X idle` and ask before long
    automated sessions while they're at the PC.
  - Ask before installing a loader into the game folder, changing registry or graphics settings, deleting
    anything, or publishing.

## References
- `references/engines/`:
  - big engines: `unity.md`, `unreal.md`, `godot.md`, `source.md`, `native.md`;
  - families and frameworks: `dotnet-xna.md` (Terraria, Stardew, Celeste), `bethesda.md`,
    `iw-engine.md` (Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare and World at War: IW 3.0/T4),
    `big-frameworks.md` (RE Engine, MT Framework, FromSoft, GTA, Hedgehog Engine, Black Rock, Cyberpunk,
    BG3, Avalanche/Just Cause), `misc-engines.md` (GameMaker, RPG Maker, Ren'Py, Paradox, Doom, HTML5, LÖVE,
    Java, Dwarf Fortress), `zengin.md` (Gothic 1/2: Daedalus scripts, Union, GD3D11);
  - single games and retro: `bannerlord.md` (Mount & Blade II: modules, XML/XSLT, C# SubModules, Harmony),
    `minecraft.md`, `genie-aoe2.md`, `isaac.md` (Binding of Isaac: Lua mods, REPENTOGON, anm2, console),
    `retro-decomp.md`.
- `references/case-studies.md`: Terraria, AoE2 and Minecraft × GTA V end to end, every non-obvious fact.
- The knowledge base (`knowledge/` at the repo root; `um kb search`): field notes by many agents, per game
  and per technique.
- `references/safety.md`: the rules with their reasons, anti-cheat and legal hygiene.

===hook
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# SessionStart hook: put universal-modder's bin/ on PATH for every later Bash call in the session,
     3	# so skills can just say `um ...`. Arg 1: the toolkit root (plugin root or the cloned repo).
     4	root="${1:-${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}}}"
     5	# Windows (Git Bash): the root arrives as C:/..., whose colon would split PATH into "C" and "/Users/...".
     6	[ -n "$root" ] && command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1 && root="$(cygpath -u "$root")"
     7	[ -n "$root" ] && [ -n "${CLAUDE_ENV_FILE:-}" ] && [ -x "$root/bin/um" ] || exit 0
     8	grep -qs "universal-modder-path" "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE" && exit 0
     9	printf 'export PATH="%s/bin:$PATH"  # universal-modder-path\n' "$root" >> "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE"
    10	exit 0
===bin/um
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# universal-modder CLI launcher. Works from a clone, a Claude Code plugin install, or a PATH symlink.
     3	#   um scan --list | um fal sprite "..." | um sprite cutout in.png out.png | um video compile edl.json out.mp4 ...
     4	# Uses uv when available (it creates the project's .venv with Pillow + numpy on first run);
     5	# otherwise the system python3, which then needs `pip install pillow numpy`.
     6	set -euo pipefail
     7	SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
     8	while [ -L "$SRC" ]; do
     9	  DIR="$(cd -P "$(dirname "$SRC")" && pwd)"
    10	  SRC="$(readlink "$SRC")"
    11	  [[ "$SRC" != /* ]] && SRC="$DIR/$SRC"
    12	done
    13	ROOT="$(cd -P "$(dirname "$SRC")/.." && pwd)"
    14	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -z "${UM_NO_UV:-}" ]; then
    15	  exec uv run --quiet --project "$ROOT" python -m um "$@"
    16	fi
    17	PY="$(command -v python3 || command -v python)"
    18	PYTHONPATH="$ROOT${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" exec "$PY" -m um "$@"

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# SessionStart hook: put universal-modder's bin/ on PATH for every later Bash call in the session,
     3	# so skills can just say `um ...`. Arg 1: the toolkit root (plugin root or the cloned repo).
     4	root="${1:-${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}}}"
     5	# Windows (Git Bash): the root arrives as C:/..., whose colon would split PATH into "C" and "/Users/...".
     6	[ -n "$root" ] && command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1 && root="$(cygpath -u "$root")"
     7	[ -n "$root" ] && [ -n "${CLAUDE_ENV_FILE:-}" ] && [ -x "$root/bin/um" ] || exit 0
     8	grep -qs "universal-modder-path" "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE" && exit 0
     9	printf 'export PATH="%s/bin:$PATH"  # universal-modder-path\n' "$root" >> "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE"
    10	exit 0
===bin/um
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# universal-modder CLI launcher. Works from a clone, a Claude Code plugin install, or a PATH symlink.
     3	#   um scan --list | um fal sprite "..." | um sprite cutout in.png out.png | um video compile edl.json out.mp4 ...
     4	# Uses uv when available (it creates the project's .venv with Pillow + numpy on first run);
     5	# otherwise the system python3, which then needs `pip install pillow numpy`.
     6	set -euo pipefail
     7	SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
     8	while [ -L "$SRC" ]; do
     9	  DIR="$(cd -P "$(dirname "$SRC")" && pwd)"
    10	  SRC="$(readlink "$SRC")"
    11	  [[ "$SRC" != /* ]] && SRC="$DIR/$SRC"
    12	done
    13	ROOT="$(cd -P "$(dirname "$SRC")/.." && pwd)"
    14	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -z "${UM_NO_UV:-}" ]; then
    15	  exec uv run --quiet --project "$ROOT" python -m um "$@"
    16	fi
    17	PY="$(command -v python3 || command -v python)"
    18	PYTHONPATH="$ROOT${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" exec "$PY" -m um "$@"

"""The knowledge base: field notes on how games were actually modded, written by agents for agents.

    um kb search "unreal pak mod"               # prior art before you start (local repo, or synced from GitHub)
    um kb search terraria --route loader-api    # filter by game / engine / route
    um kb show games/terraria/fal-arsenal.md
    um kb new --game "Hades II" --title "A new boon god" --from-scan "hades"   # scaffold a note, pre-filled
    um kb check knowledge/games/hades-ii/new-boon-god.md                       # validate before a PR
    um kb index                                  # regenerate knowledge/INDEX.md + index.json
    um kb sync                                   # refresh the cached copy from GitHub
    um kb pr knowledge/games/hades-ii/new-boon-god.md --yes                     # branch, commit, push to your fork, open a PR

Every note is Markdown with YAML front matter (knowledge/TEMPLATE.md). `check` enforces the schema, the
required sections, no secrets, no pasted decompiled code, no huge files. Contributions go through pull
requests: that's how one agent's hard-won gotchas reach the next one. Ask your human before `um kb pr --yes`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

from um.common import data_dir, die, need, text_utf8

REPO = os.environ.get("UM_KB_REPO", "rehan-remade/universal-modder")
BRANCH = os.environ.get("UM_KB_BRANCH", "main")
ROUTES = ["data", "asset-only", "loader-api", "managed-patch", "native-hook", "reimplementation", "decomp-recomp",
          "passthrough", "emulator", "other"]
STATUSES = ["idea", "in-progress", "working", "released", "abandoned"]
PLATFORMS = ["windows", "linux", "macos", "proton", "emulator", "console", "other"]
GAME_KEYS = ["kind", "title", "game", "engine", "route", "status", "date", "agents"]
TECH_KEYS = ["kind", "title", "tags", "date", "agents"]
LIST_KEYS = ["games_also", "tools", "agents", "humans", "links", "tags"]
GAME_SECTIONS = ["setup", "route", "verification", "gotchas"]
MAX_BLOCK_WARN, MAX_BLOCK_FAIL = 60, 150
MAX_NOTE_KB, MAX_MEDIA_MB = 120, 1.5
# Notes and the index are UTF-8 with \n line ends on every OS. Without this, Windows reads and writes them in its
# ANSI code page with \r\n: the index's "·" separators come out as invalid UTF-8 and `um kb check --index` fails.
TEXT = {"encoding": "utf-8", "newline": "\n"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- where the notes are

def local_root() -> Path | None:
    """knowledge/ of the repo this package runs from (clone, plugin, editable install), or of the cwd's repo."""
    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "knowledge"
    if (here / "TEMPLATE.md").exists():
        return here
    for d in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents]:
        if (d / "knowledge" / "TEMPLATE.md").exists():
            return d / "knowledge"
    return None


def cache_root() -> Path:
    return data_dir() / "kb" / REPO.replace("/", "__") / "knowledge"


def sync(quiet: bool = False) -> Path:
    """Mirror knowledge/ from GitHub into the cache (git tree API + raw files; no auth needed)."""
    api = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{REPO}/git/trees/{BRANCH}?recursive=1"
    req = urllib.request.Request(api, headers={"User-Agent": "universal-modder", "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"})
    tree = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60))
    paths = [t["path"] for t in tree.get("tree", []) if t["type"] == "blob" and t["path"].startswith("knowledge/")
             and t["path"].endswith((".md", ".json"))]
    root = cache_root()
    tmp = root.with_name("knowledge.tmp")
    shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
    for p in paths:
        dst = tmp / p[len("knowledge/"):]
        dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        url = f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{REPO}/{BRANCH}/{p}"
        with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "universal-modder"}), timeout=60) as r:
            dst.write_bytes(r.read())
    shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)
    tmp.rename(root)
    (root / ".synced").write_text(str(time.time()), **TEXT)
    if not quiet:
        print(f"synced {len(paths)} files from github.com/{REPO} -> {root}")
    return root


def resolve_root(explicit: str | None = None, remote: bool = False) -> Path:
    if explicit:
        return Path(explicit)
    if os.environ.get("UM_KB"):
        return Path(os.environ["UM_KB"])
    loc = None if remote else local_root()
    if loc:
        return loc
    root = cache_root()
    stamp = root / ".synced"
    stale = not stamp.exists() or time.time() - float(stamp.read_text(encoding="utf-8") or 0) > 86400
    if stale:
        try:
            return sync(quiet=True)
        except OSError as e:
            if not root.exists():
                die(f"no local knowledge/ and GitHub sync failed ({e}); clone https://github.com/{REPO}")
    return root


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- notes

def parse(path: Path) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    m = re.match(r"^---\s*\n(.*?)\n---\s*\n?(.*)$", text, re.S)
    if not m:
        return {}, text
    yaml = need("yaml", "pyyaml")
    try:
        meta = yaml.safe_load(m.group(1)) or {}
    except (yaml.YAMLError, ValueError) as e:  # ValueError: a date YAML can't build, e.g. 2026-09-31
        return {"_yaml_error": str(e)}, m.group(2)
    return (meta if isinstance(meta, dict) else {}), m.group(2)


def notes(root: Path) -> list[tuple[Path, dict, str]]:
    out = []
    for p in sorted(root.rglob("*.md")):

1	---
2	name: minecraft-modding
3	description: "Create, modify, debug, or migrate Minecraft mods for current NeoForge or Fabric 26.x, legacy 1.21.x, and Forge 1.20.1. Use for loader-based gameplay code and assets; use minecraft-multiloader when one codebase must target both modern loaders."
4	---
5	
6	# Minecraft Modding Skill
7	
8	## Overview
9	
10	Supported platforms:
11	
12	| Platform | MC Version | Java | Build System |
13	|---|---|---|---|
14	| **NeoForge** | 26.x current; 1.21.11 examples retained | Java 25 current; Java 21 on 1.21.x | Gradle + ModDevGradle |
15	| **Forge** | 1.20.1 legacy lane | Java 17 | Gradle + ForgeGradle 6 |
16	| **Fabric** | 26.x current; 1.21.11 examples retained | Java 25 current; Java 21 on 1.21.x | Gradle + Fabric Loom |
17	| **Architectury** (multiloader) | 26.x or 1.21.x | Match Minecraft | Gradle + Architectury Loom |
18	
19	Always confirm the platform and Minecraft version from `gradle.properties` or `build.gradle`
20	before writing any mod-specific code.
21	
22	Minecraft 26.1 introduced Java 25 and unobfuscated game executables. For 26.x
23	projects, start from the current loader generator or example mod and preserve
24	its build layout. Do not copy the 1.21.11 mapping, Loom plugin, remapping task,
25	or Java 21 snippets in this skill into a 26.x project. Fabric 26.x uses the
26	non-remapping Loom path and official names; NeoForge 26.x should start from the
27	current NeoForge generator. The detailed API references cover legacy 1.21.x
28	examples unless a section explicitly says 26.x.
29	
30	### Routing Boundaries
31	- `Use when`: the task is Java/Kotlin mod code, registry/event work, networking, datagen wiring, and loader APIs.
32	- `Do not use when`: the task is command-only vanilla logic (`minecraft-commands-scripting`) or pure datapacks (`minecraft-datapack`).
33	- `Do not use when`: the task targets Paper/Bukkit plugins (`minecraft-plugin-dev`).
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 1. Identifying the Platform
38	
39	```bash
40	# NeoForge project signature
41	grep -r "net.neoforged" gradle.properties build.gradle settings.gradle 2>/dev/null | head -5
42	
43	# Forge 1.20.1 project signature
44	grep -r "net.minecraftforge" gradle.properties build.gradle settings.gradle 2>/dev/null | head -5
45	
46	# Fabric project signature
47	grep -r "fabric" gradle.properties build.gradle settings.gradle 2>/dev/null | head -5
48	
49	# Read mod ID and version
50	cat gradle.properties
51	```
52	
53	Key files per platform:
54	
55	- **NeoForge**: `src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml`, annotated `@Mod` main class
56	- **Forge 1.20.1**: `src/main/resources/META-INF/mods.toml`, `net.minecraftforge:forge` dependency
57	- **Fabric**: `src/main/resources/fabric.mod.json`, class implementing `ModInitializer`
58	- **Architectury**: `common/`, `fabric/`, `neoforge/` subprojects
59	
60	---
61	
62	## 2. Build & Test Commands
63	
64	```bash
65	# Build the mod jar
66	./gradlew build
67	
68	# Run the Minecraft client to test
69	./gradlew runClient
70	
71	# Run a dedicated server to test
72	./gradlew runServer
73	
74	# NeoForge Game Tests (when the project configures this run)
75	./gradlew runGameTestServer
76	
77	# Current NeoForge MDK data generation; Fabric/Forge use their configured task
78	./gradlew runClientData
79	
80	# Remove this project's generated build outputs before a fresh rebuild
81	./gradlew clean
82	
83	# Only if the project applies a dependency-updates plugin
84	./gradlew dependencyUpdates
85	```
86	
87	`./gradlew build` runs the project's configured build tasks. Candidate mod jars are
88	usually under `build/libs/`, but task names and file names are project-specific.
89	Check the build result, then identify the intended
90	distributable before publishing it.
91	
92	---
93	
94	## 3. Project Layout (NeoForge)
95	
96	```
97	src/
98	  main/
99	    java/<groupId>/<modid>/
100	      MyMod.java               ← @Mod entry point
101	      block/
102	        ModBlocks.java         ← DeferredRegister.Blocks
103	        MyCustomBlock.java
104	      item/
105	        ModItems.java          ← DeferredRegister.Items
106	      entity/
107	        ModEntities.java       ← DeferredRegister.Entities
108	      menu/                    ← custom GUI containers
109	      recipe/
110	      worldgen/
111	      datagen/
112	        ModDataGen.java        ← GatherDataEvent handler
113	        providers/
114	    resources/
115	      META-INF/
116	        neoforge.mods.toml     ← mod metadata (renamed from mods.toml in NeoForge 1.20.5+)
117	      assets/<modid>/
118	        blockstates/           ← JSON blockstate definitions
119	        models/
120	          block/               ← block model JSON
121	          item/                ← item model JSON
122	        items/                 ← 1.21.4+ item-definition JSON
123	        textures/
124	          block/               ← 16×16 PNG textures
125	          item/
126	        lang/
127	          en_us.json           ← translation strings
128	      data/<modid>/
129	        recipe/                ← crafting recipe JSON (26.x)
130	        loot_table/
131	          blocks/              ← per-block loot table JSON
132	        tags/
133	          block/
134	          item/
135	```
136	
137	## 4. Project Layout (Forge 1.20.1)
138	
139	Use this layout only when `minecraft_version=1.20.1` and the project depends on
140	`net.minecraftforge:forge`. Forge 1.20.1 is not NeoForge: keep `mods.toml`,
141	`net.minecraftforge.*` imports, Java 17, and ForgeGradle 6 patterns.
142	
143	```
144	src/
145	  main/
146	    java/<groupId>/<modid>/
147	      MyMod.java               <- @Mod entry point
148	      block/
149	        ModBlocks.java         <- DeferredRegister<Block>
150	      item/
151	        ModItems.java          <- DeferredRegister<Item>
152	      datagen/
153	        ModDataGen.java        <- GatherDataEvent handler
154	    resources/
155	      META-INF/
156	        mods.toml              <- Forge metadata
157	      assets/<modid>/          <- client assets
158	      data/<modid>/            <- server data using 1.20.1 paths
159	```
160	
161	See `references/forge-1.20.1-api.md` before editing Forge 1.20.1 projects.
162	
163	## 5. Project Layout (Fabric)
164	
165	```
166	src/
167	  main/
168	    java/<groupId>/<modid>/
169	      MyMod.java               ← implements ModInitializer
170	      client/
171	        MyModClient.java       ← implements ClientModInitializer
172	      block/
173	      item/
174	      mixin/                   ← Mixin classes
175	    resources/
176	      fabric.mod.json
177	      assets/<modid>/          ← same as NeoForge
178	      data/<modid>/            ← same as NeoForge
179	      <modid>.mixins.json      ← mixin configuration
180	```
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 6. Core Concepts Cheatsheet
185	
186	### Sides
187	- **Physical client** – the game client JAR (has rendering code)
188	- **Physical server** – the dedicated server JAR (no rendering)
189	- **Logical client** – the client thread (handles rendering, input)
190	- **Logical server** – the server thread (handles world simulation)
191	- Keep rendering classes in a client-only initializer or listener. A logical-side
192	  check alone does not prevent dedicated servers from loading client classes.
193	  Follow the loader's [physical-side guidance](https://docs.neoforged.net/docs/1.21.11/concepts/sides/).
194	
195	### Registries
196	Everything in Minecraft lives in a registry. Always register objects; never
197	construct them at field initializer time outside a registry call. Use the
198	mapping-appropriate registry constants for the loader you are editing:
199	
200	| Type | NeoForge / Mojang mappings | Fabric / Yarn mappings |
201	|------|-----------------------------|-------------------------|
202	| Blocks | `BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK` | `Registries.BLOCK` |
203	| Items | `BuiltInRegistries.ITEM` | `Registries.ITEM` |
204	| Entity types | `BuiltInRegistries.ENTITY_TYPE` | `Registries.ENTITY_TYPE` |
205	| Block entity types | `BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK_ENTITY_TYPE` | `Registries.BLOCK_ENTITY_TYPE` |
206	| Menu / screen-handler types | `BuiltInRegistries.MENU` | `Registries.SCREEN_HANDLER` |
207	| Sound events | `BuiltInRegistries.SOUND_EVENT` | `Registries.SOUND_EVENT` |
208	| Biomes | `Registries.BIOME` registry keys | `RegistryKeys.BIOME` registry keys |
209	
210	Do not copy older `Registry.BLOCK` / `Registry.ITEM` constants into 1.21.x code;
211	those names are stale for the examples in this skill.
212	
213	### ResourceLocation / Identifier
214	Every registry entry needs a namespaced ID:
215	```java
216	// 26.x official names (NeoForge and Fabric)
217	Identifier id = Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath("mymod", "my_block");
218	
219	// Older Mojang mappings use ResourceLocation; keep the project's version.
220	// Legacy Fabric with Yarn mappings
221	Identifier id = Identifier.of("mymod", "my_block");
222	```
223	
224	---
225	
226	## 7. NeoForge Quick Patterns (26.x)
227	
228	For 26.x, use the explicitly labelled 26.x sections in
229	`references/common-patterns.md` and select the project's exact version in the
230	[NeoForge documentation](https://docs.neoforged.net/docs/gettingstarted/).
231	`references/neoforge-api.md` contains legacy 1.21.x / Java 21 patterns only;
232	do not copy its dependency pins into a 26.x project.
233	
234	```java
235	// Main mod class
236	@Mod(MyMod.MOD_ID)
237	public class MyMod {
238	    public static final String MOD_ID = "mymod";
239	
240	    public MyMod(IEventBus modEventBus) {
241	        ModBlocks.BLOCKS.register(modEventBus);
242	        ModItems.ITEMS.register(modEventBus);
243	        modEventBus.addListener(this::commonSetup);
244	    }
245	
246	    private void commonSetup(FMLCommonSetupEvent event) {
247	        // runs after all mods are registered
248	    }
249	}
250	```
251	
252	```java
253	// Block registration
254	public class ModBlocks {
255	    public static final DeferredRegister.Blocks BLOCKS =
256	        DeferredRegister.createBlocks(MyMod.MOD_ID);
257	
258	    public static final DeferredBlock<Block> MY_BLOCK =
259	        BLOCKS.registerSimpleBlock("my_block", () ->
260	            BlockBehaviour.Properties.of()
261	                .mapColor(MapColor.STONE)
262	                .strength(1.5f, 6.0f)
263	                .sound(SoundType.STONE)
264	                .requiresCorrectToolForDrops());
265	}
266	```
267	
268	---
269	
270	## 8. Forge 1.20.1 Quick Patterns
271	
272	See full patterns in `references/forge-1.20.1-api.md`.
273	
274	```java
275	// Main mod class
276	@Mod(MyMod.MOD_ID)
277	public class MyMod {
278	    public static final String MOD_ID = "mymod";
279	
280	    public MyMod(FMLJavaModLoadingContext context) {
281	        IEventBus modEventBus = context.getModEventBus();
282	        ModBlocks.BLOCKS.register(modEventBus);
283	        ModItems.ITEMS.register(modEventBus);
284	        modEventBus.addListener(this::commonSetup);
285	        MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this);
286	    }
287	
288	    private void commonSetup(FMLCommonSetupEvent event) {
289	        // runs after registries are prepared
290	    }
291	}
292	```
293	
294	```java
295	// Block registration
296	public class ModBlocks {
297	    public static final DeferredRegister<Block> BLOCKS =
298	        DeferredRegister.create(ForgeRegistries.BLOCKS, MyMod.MOD_ID);
299	
300	    public static final RegistryObject<Block> MY_BLOCK =
301	        BLOCKS.register("my_block", () -> new Block(
302	            BlockBehaviour.Properties.of()
303	                .mapColor(MapColor.STONE)
304	                .strength(1.5f, 6.0f)
305	                .sound(SoundType.STONE)
306	                .requiresCorrectToolForDrops()));
307	}
308	```
309	
310	---
311	## 9. Fabric Quick Patterns
312	
313	Match the project's Minecraft version and mappings in the
314	[Fabric documentation](https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/).
315	`references/fabric-api.md` contains legacy 1.21.x / Java 21 patterns only.
316	The explicitly labelled 26.x sections in `references/common-patterns.md`
317	use NeoForge syntax; adapt them against the exact Fabric API rather than
318	copying loader-specific classes or legacy dependency pins.
319	
320	```java
321	// Main mod class
322	public class MyMod implements ModInitializer {
323	    public static final String MOD_ID = "mymod";
324	    public static final Logger LOGGER = LoggerFactory.getLogger(MOD_ID);
325	
326	    @Override
327	    public void onInitialize() {
328	        ModBlocks.initialize();
329	        ModItems.register();
330	    }
331	}
332	```
333	
334	```java
335	// Fabric 26.x with official Mojang mappings. Create the key before the object
336	// so its properties receive the required id during construction.
337	public final class ModBlocks {
338	    public static final ResourceKey<Block> MY_BLOCK_KEY = ResourceKey.create(
339	        Registries.BLOCK,
340	        Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath(MyMod.MOD_ID, "my_block")
341	    );
342	
343	    public static final Block MY_BLOCK = register(
344	        MY_BLOCK_KEY,
345	        Block::new,
346	        BlockBehaviour.Properties.of()
347	            .mapColor(MapColor.STONE)
348	            .strength(1.5f, 6.0f)
349	            .sound(SoundType.STONE)
350	            .requiresCorrectToolForDrops()
351	    );
352	
353	    private static Block register(ResourceKey<Block> key,
354	            Function<BlockBehaviour.Properties, Block> factory,
355	            BlockBehaviour.Properties properties) {
356	        Block block = factory.apply(properties.setId(key));
357	        return Registry.register(BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK, key, block);
358	    }
359	
360	    public static void initialize() {}
361	}
362	```
363	
364	Call `ModBlocks.initialize()` from the Fabric initializer. The Yarn-named
365	1.21.11 examples remain in `references/fabric-api.md`; do not mix those names
366	with this 26.x pattern.
367	
368	---
369	
370	## 10. JSON Asset Templates
371	
372	Always provide matching JSON assets for every registered block/item.
373	Codex should generate or update these files alongside Java code.
374	For Forge 1.20.1, check `references/forge-1.20.1-api.md` for legacy server-data
375	directory names before creating loot tables or tags.
376	
377	See `references/common-patterns.md` for full JSON templates for:
378	- Blockstate JSON
379	- Block model JSON (cube, slab, stairs, fence, door, trapdoor, etc.)
380	- Item model JSON
381	- Loot table JSON
382	- Recipe JSON (crafting_shaped, crafting_shapeless, smelting, blasting, stonecutting)
383	- Language file (`en_us.json`) entries
384	- Tag JSON
385	
386	---
387	
388	## 11. Data Generation
389	
390	Use the project's configured data providers. Current NeoForge uses
391	`GatherDataEvent.Client` / `.Server` and `event.createProvider(...)`; the MDK
392	normally generates both asset and data providers with `runClientData`. See the
393	[version-matched resource guide](https://docs.neoforged.net/docs/resources/)
394	before wiring providers. Keep Fabric and older projects on their own datagen
395	entrypoints and Gradle tasks, then inspect the generated files.
396	For Forge 1.20.1, use the mod-event-bus registration, `GatherDataEvent`
397	signature, provider classes, and legacy output paths from
398	`references/forge-1.20.1-api.md`.
399	
400	---
401	
402	## 12. Common Tasks Checklist
403	
404	When adding a **new block**:
405	- [ ] `Block` subclass (or use vanilla Block with properties)
406	- [ ] Register in `ModBlocks.BLOCKS` / `Registries.BLOCK`
407	- [ ] Register `BlockItem` in `ModItems.ITEMS` / `Registries.ITEM`
408	- [ ] Blockstate JSON → `assets/<modid>/blockstates/<name>.json`
409	- [ ] Block model JSON → `assets/<modid>/models/block/<name>.json`
410	- [ ] Item model JSON → `assets/<modid>/models/item/<name>.json` (or inherits from block)
411	- [ ] 1.21.4+ item definition → `assets/<modid>/items/<name>.json`, pointing at the item or block model
412	- [ ] Texture PNG → `assets/<modid>/textures/block/<name>.png`
413	- [ ] Loot table JSON -> 1.21.x: `data/<modid>/loot_table/blocks/<name>.json`; Forge 1.20.1: `data/<modid>/loot_tables/blocks/<name>.json`
414	- [ ] Tags -> 1.21.x: `data/<modid>/tags/block/` and `tags/item/`; Forge 1.20.1: `data/<modid>/tags/blocks/` and `tags/items/`
415	- [ ] Language entry in `en_us.json`
416	- [ ] Vanilla mining and tool-tier tags when `requiresCorrectToolForDrops` is set
417	- [ ] Do not mix Forge 1.20.1 plural server-data paths with 1.21.x singular server-data paths
418	
419	When adding a **new item**:
420	- [ ] `Item` subclass (or use `new Item(properties)`)
421	- [ ] Register in `ModItems` / `Registries.ITEM`
422	- [ ] Item model JSON
423	- [ ] 1.21.4+ item definition → `assets/<modid>/items/<name>.json`
424	- [ ] Texture PNG
425	- [ ] Language entry
426	- [ ] Creative tab registration (NeoForge/Forge: `BuildCreativeModeTabContentsEvent`; Fabric: `ItemGroupEvents`)
427	- [ ] Recipe JSON if craftable (`data/<modid>/recipe/` for 26.x; see the
428	      version-specific recipe reference before using a 1.21.x project)
429	
430	When adding a **new entity**:
431	- [ ] Entity class (extends appropriate base: `Mob`, `Animal`, `TamableAnimal`, etc.)
432	- [ ] `EntityType` registration
433	- [ ] Renderer and model classes loaded only on the physical client
434	- [ ] Register the renderer with `EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterRenderers` (NeoForge)
435	      or `EntityRendererRegistry` (Fabric); register model layers separately
436	- [ ] Spawn egg item (optional)
437	- [ ] Spawn rules / biome modifier
438	
439	---
440	
441	## 13. References
442	
443	- NeoForge API patterns and event system: `./references/neoforge-api.md`
444	- Forge 1.20.1 API patterns and MDK workflow: `./references/forge-1.20.1-api.md`
445	- Fabric API patterns and mixin guide: `./references/fabric-api.md`
446	- Blocks, items, recipes, commands, datagen: `./references/common-patterns.md`
447	- NeoForge official docs: https://docs.neoforged.net/
448	- Fabric developer docs: https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/
449	- Architectury (multiloader): https://docs.architectury.dev/
450	- Minecraft Wiki (data formats): https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_data_values
