file.content:
---
name: minecraft-modding
description: "Create, modify, debug, or migrate Minecraft mods for current NeoForge or Fabric 26.x, legacy 1.21.x, and Forge 1.20.1. Use for loader-based gameplay code and assets; use minecraft-multiloader when one codebase must target both modern loaders."
---

# Minecraft Modding Skill

## Overview

Supported platforms:

| Platform | MC Version | Java | Build System |
|---|---|---|---|
| **NeoForge** | 26.x current; 1.21.11 examples retained | Java 25 current; Java 21 on 1.21.x | Gradle + ModDevGradle |
| **Forge** | 1.20.1 legacy lane | Java 17 | Gradle + ForgeGradle 6 |
| **Fabric** | 26.x current; 1.21.11 examples retained | Java 25 current; Java 21 on 1.21.x | Gradle + Fabric Loom |
| **Architectury** (multiloader) | 26.x or 1.21.x | Match Minecraft | Gradle + Architectury Loom |

Always confirm the platform and Minecraft version from `gradle.properties` or `build.gradle`
before writing any mod-specific code.

Minecraft 26.1 introduced Java 25 and unobfuscated game executables. For 26.x
projects, start from the current loader generator or example mod and preserve
its build layout. Do not copy the 1.21.11 mapping, Loom plugin, remapping task,
or Java 21 snippets in this skill into a 26.x project. Fabric 26.x uses the
non-remapping Loom path and official names; NeoForge 26.x should start from the
current NeoForge generator. The detailed API references cover legacy 1.21.x
examples unless a section explicitly says 26.x.

### Routing Boundaries
- `Use when`: the task is Java/Kotlin mod code, registry/event work, networking, datagen wiring, and loader APIs.
- `Do not use when`: the task is command-only vanilla logic (`minecraft-commands-scripting`) or pure datapacks (`minecraft-datapack`).
- `Do not use when`: the task targets Paper/Bukkit plugins (`minecraft-plugin-dev`).

---

## 1. Identifying the Platform

```bash
# NeoForge project signature
grep -r "net.neoforged" gradle.properties build.gradle settings.gradle 2>/dev/null | head -5

# Forge 1.20.1 project signature
grep -r "net.minecraftforge" gradle.properties build.gradle settings.gradle 2>/dev/null | head -5

# Fabric project signature
grep -r "fabric" gradle.properties build.gradle settings.gradle 2>/dev/null | head -5

# Read mod ID and version
cat gradle.properties
```

Key files per platform:

- **NeoForge**: `src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml`, annotated `@Mod` main class
- **Forge 1.20.1**: `src/main/resources/META-INF/mods.toml`, `net.minecraftforge:forge` dependency
- **Fabric**: `src/main/resources/fabric.mod.json`, class implementing `ModInitializer`
- **Architectury**: `common/`, `fabric/`, `neoforge/` subprojects

---

## 2. Build & Test Commands

```bash
# Build the mod jar
./gradlew build

# Run the Minecraft client to test
./gradlew runClient

# Run a dedicated server to test
./gradlew runServer

# NeoForge Game Tests (when the project configures this run)
./gradlew runGameTestServer

# Current NeoForge MDK data generation; Fabric/Forge use their configured task
./gradlew runClientData

# Remove this project's generated build outputs before a fresh rebuild
./gradlew clean

# Only if the project applies a dependency-updates plugin
./gradlew dependencyUpdates
```

`./gradlew build` runs the project's configured build tasks. Candidate mod jars are
usually under `build/libs/`, but task names and file names are project-specific.
Check the build result, then identify the intended
distributable before publishing it.

---

## 3. Project Layout (NeoForge)

```
src/
  main/
    java/<groupId>/<modid>/
      MyMod.java               ← @Mod entry point
      block/
        ModBlocks.java         ← DeferredRegister.Blocks
        MyCustomBlock.java
      item/
        ModItems.java          ← DeferredRegister.Items
      entity/
        ModEntities.java       ← DeferredRegister.Entities
      menu/                    ← custom GUI containers
      recipe/
      worldgen/
      datagen/
        ModDataGen.java        ← GatherDataEvent handler
        providers/
    resources/
      META-INF/
        neoforge.mods.toml     ← mod metadata (renamed from mods.toml in NeoForge 1.20.5+)
      assets/<modid>/
        blockstates/           ← JSON blockstate definitions
        models/
          block/               ← block model JSON
          item/                ← item model JSON
        items/                 ← 1.21.4+ item-definition JSON
        textures/
          block/               ← 16×16 PNG textures
          item/
        lang/
          en_us.json           ← translation strings
      data/<modid>/
        recipe/                ← crafting recipe JSON (26.x)
        loot_table/
          blocks/              ← per-block loot table JSON
        tags/
          block/
          item/
```

## 4. Project Layout (Forge 1.20.1)

Use this layout only when `minecraft_version=1.20.1` and the project depends on
`net.minecraftforge:forge`. Forge 1.20.1 is not NeoForge: keep `mods.toml`,
`net.minecraftforge.*` imports, Java 17, and ForgeGradle 6 patterns.

```
src/
  main/
    java/<groupId>/<modid>/
      MyMod.java               <- @Mod entry point
      block/
        ModBlocks.java         <- DeferredRegister<Block>
      item/
        ModItems.java          <- DeferredRegister<Item>
      datagen/
        ModDataGen.java        <- GatherDataEvent handler
    resources/
      META-INF/
        mods.toml              <- Forge metadata
      assets/<modid>/          <- client assets
      data/<modid>/            <- server data using 1.20.1 paths
```

See `references/forge-1.20.1-api.md` before editing Forge 1.20.1 projects.

## 5. Project Layout (Fabric)

```
src/
  main/
    java/<groupId>/<modid>/
      MyMod.java               ← implements ModInitializer
      client/
        MyModClient.java       ← implements ClientModInitializer
      block/
      item/
      mixin/                   ← Mixin classes
    resources/
      fabric.mod.json
      assets/<modid>/          ← same as NeoForge
      data/<modid>/            ← same as NeoForge
      <modid>.mixins.json      ← mixin configuration
```

---

## 6. Core Concepts Cheatsheet

### Sides
- **Physical client** – the game client JAR (has rendering code)
- **Physical server** – the dedicated server JAR (no rendering)
- **Logical client** – the client thread (handles rendering, input)
- **Logical server** – the server thread (handles world simulation)
- Keep rendering classes in a client-only initializer or listener. A logical-side
  check alone does not prevent dedicated servers from loading client classes.
  Follow the loader's [physical-side guidance](https://docs.neoforged.net/docs/1.21.11/concepts/sides/).

### Registries
Everything in Minecraft lives in a registry. Always register objects; never
construct them at field initializer time outside a registry call. Use the
mapping-appropriate registry constants for the loader you are editing:

| Type | NeoForge / Mojang mappings | Fabric / Yarn mappings |
|------|-----------------------------|-------------------------|
| Blocks | `BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK` | `Registries.BLOCK` |
| Items | `BuiltInRegistries.ITEM` | `Registries.ITEM` |
| Entity types | `BuiltInRegistries.ENTITY_TYPE` | `Registries.ENTITY_TYPE` |
| Block entity types | `BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK_ENTITY_TYPE` | `Registries.BLOCK_ENTITY_TYPE` |
| Menu / screen-handler types | `BuiltInRegistries.MENU` | `Registries.SCREEN_HANDLER` |
| Sound events | `BuiltInRegistries.SOUND_EVENT` | `Registries.SOUND_EVENT` |
| Biomes | `Registries.BIOME` registry keys | `RegistryKeys.BIOME` registry keys |

Do not copy older `Registry.BLOCK` / `Registry.ITEM` constants into 1.21.x code;
those names are stale for the examples in this skill.

### ResourceLocation / Identifier
Every registry entry needs a namespaced ID:
```java
// 26.x official names (NeoForge and Fabric)
Identifier id = Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath("mymod", "my_block");

// Older Mojang mappings use ResourceLocation; keep the project's version.
// Legacy Fabric with Yarn mappings
Identifier id = Identifier.of("mymod", "my_block");
```

---

## 7. NeoForge Quick Patterns (26.x)

For 26.x, use the explicitly labelled 26.x sections in
`references/common-patterns.md` and select the project's exact version in the
[NeoForge documentation](https://docs.neoforged.net/docs/gettingstarted/).
`references/neoforge-api.md` contains legacy 1.21.x / Java 21 patterns only;
do not copy its dependency pins into a 26.x project.

```java
// Main mod class
@Mod(MyMod.MOD_ID)
public class MyMod {
    public static final String MOD_ID = "mymod";

    public MyMod(IEventBus modEventBus) {
        ModBlocks.BLOCKS.register(modEventBus);
        ModItems.ITEMS.register(modEventBus);
        modEventBus.addListener(this::commonSetup);
    }

    private void commonSetup(FMLCommonSetupEvent event) {
        // runs after all mods are registered
    }
}
```

```java
// Block registration
public class ModBlocks {
    public static final DeferredRegister.Blocks BLOCKS =
        DeferredRegister.createBlocks(MyMod.MOD_ID);

    public static final DeferredBlock<Block> MY_BLOCK =
        BLOCKS.registerSimpleBlock("my_block", () ->
            BlockBehaviour.Properties.of()
                .mapColor(MapColor.STONE)
                .strength(1.5f, 6.0f)
                .sound(SoundType.STONE)
                .requiresCorrectToolForDrops());
}
```

---

## 8. Forge 1.20.1 Quick Patterns

See full patterns in `references/forge-1.20.1-api.md`.

```java
// Main mod class
@Mod(MyMod.MOD_ID)
public class MyMod {
    public static final String MOD_ID = "mymod";

    public MyMod(FMLJavaModLoadingContext context) {
        IEventBus modEventBus = context.getModEventBus();
        ModBlocks.BLOCKS.register(modEventBus);
        ModItems.ITEMS.register(modEventBus);
        modEventBus.addListener(this::commonSetup);
        MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this);
    }

    private void commonSetup(FMLCommonSetupEvent event) {
        // runs after registries are prepared
    }
}
```

```java
// Block registration
public class ModBlocks {
    public static final DeferredRegister<Block> BLOCKS =
        DeferredRegister.create(ForgeRegistries.BLOCKS, MyMod.MOD_ID);

    public static final RegistryObject<Block> MY_BLOCK =
        BLOCKS.register("my_block", () -> new Block(
            BlockBehaviour.Properties.of()
                .mapColor(MapColor.STONE)
                .strength(1.5f, 6.0f)
                .sound(SoundType.STONE)
                .requiresCorrectToolForDrops()));
}
```

---
## 9. Fabric Quick Patterns

Match the project's Minecraft version and mappings in the
[Fabric documentation](https://docs.fabricmc.net/develop/).
`references/fabric-api.md` contains legacy 1.21.x / Java 21 patterns only.
The explicitly labelled 26.x sections in `references/common-patterns.md`
use NeoForge syntax; adapt them against the exact Fabric API rather than
copying loader-specific classes or legacy dependency pins.

```java
// Main mod class
public class MyMod implements ModInitializer {
    public static final String MOD_ID = "mymod";
    public static final Logger LOGGER = LoggerFactory.getLogger(MOD_ID);

    @Override
    public void onInitialize() {
        ModBlocks.initialize();
        ModItems.register();
    }
}
```

```java
// Fabric 26.x with official Mojang mappings. Create the key before the object
// so its properties receive the required id during construction.
public final class ModBlocks {
    public static final ResourceKey<Block> MY_BLOCK_KEY = ResourceKey.create(
        Registries.BLOCK,
        Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath(MyMod.MOD_ID, "my_block")
    );

    public static final Block MY_BLOCK = register(
        MY_BLOCK_KEY,
        Block::new,
        BlockBehaviour.Properties.of()
            .mapColor(MapColor.STONE)
            .strength(1.5f, 6.0f)
            .sound(SoundType.STONE)
            .requiresCorrectToolForDrops()
    );

    private static Block register(ResourceKey<Block> key,
            Function<BlockBehaviour.Properties, Block> factory,
            BlockBehaviour.Properties properties) {
        Block block = factory.apply(properties.setId(key));
        return Registry.register(BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK, key, block);
    }

    public static void initialize() {}
}
```

Call `ModBlocks.initialize()` from the Fabric initializer. The Yarn-named
1.21.11 examples remain in `references/fabric-api.md`; do not mix those names
with this 26.x pattern.

---

## 10. JSON Asset Templates

Always provide matching JSON assets for every registered block/item.
Codex should generate or update these files alongside Java code.
For Forge 1.20.1, check `references/forge-1.20.1-api.md` for legacy server-data
directory names before creating loot tables or tags.

See `references/common-patterns.md` for full JSON templates for:
- Blockstate JSON
- Block model JSON (cube, slab, stairs, fence, door, trapdoor, etc.)
- Item model JSON
- Loot table JSON
- Recipe JSON (crafting_shaped, crafting_shapeless, smelting, blasting, stonecutting)
- Language file (`en_us.json`) entries
- Tag JSON

---

## 11. Data Generation

Use the project's configured data providers. Current NeoForge uses
`GatherDataEvent.Client` / `.Server` and `event.createProvider(...)`; the MDK
normally generates both asset and data providers with `runClientData`. See the
[version-matched resource guide](https://docs.neoforged.net/docs/resources/)
before wiring providers. Keep Fabric and older projects on their own datagen
entrypoints and Gradle tasks, then inspect the generated files.
For Forge 1.20.1, use the mod-event-bus registration, `GatherDataEvent`
signature, provider classes, and legacy output paths from
`references/forge-1.20.1-api.md`.

---

## 12. Common Tasks Checklist

When adding a **new block**:
- [ ] `Block` subclass (or use vanilla Block with properties)
- [ ] Register in `ModBlocks.BLOCKS` / `Registries.BLOCK`
- [ ] Register `BlockItem` in `ModItems.ITEMS` / `Registries.ITEM`
- [ ] Blockstate JSON → `assets/<modid>/blockstates/<name>.json`
- [ ] Block model JSON → `assets/<modid>/models/block/<name>.json`
- [ ] Item model JSON → `assets/<modid>/models/item/<name>.json` (or inherits from block)
- [ ] 1.21.4+ item definition → `assets/<modid>/items/<name>.json`, pointing at the item or block model
- [ ] Texture PNG → `assets/<modid>/textures/block/<name>.png`
- [ ] Loot table JSON -> 1.21.x: `data/<modid>/loot_table/blocks/<name>.json`; Forge 1.20.1: `data/<modid>/loot_tables/blocks/<name>.json`
- [ ] Tags -> 1.21.x: `data/<modid>/tags/block/` and `tags/item/`; Forge 1.20.1: `data/<modid>/tags/blocks/` and `tags/items/`
- [ ] Language entry in `en_us.json`
- [ ] Vanilla mining and tool-tier tags when `requiresCorrectToolForDrops` is set
- [ ] Do not mix Forge 1.20.1 plural server-data paths with 1.21.x singular server-data paths

When adding a **new item**:
- [ ] `Item` subclass (or use `new Item(properties)`)
- [ ] Register in `ModItems` / `Registries.ITEM`
- [ ] Item model JSON
- [ ] 1.21.4+ item definition → `assets/<modid>/items/<name>.json`
- [ ] Texture PNG
- [ ] Language entry
- [ ] Creative tab registration (NeoForge/Forge: `BuildCreativeModeTabContentsEvent`; Fabric: `ItemGroupEvents`)
- [ ] Recipe JSON if craftable (`data/<modid>/recipe/` for 26.x; see the
      version-specific recipe reference before using a 1.21.x project)

When adding a **new entity**:
- [ ] Entity class (extends appropriate base: `Mob`, `Animal`, `TamableAnimal`, etc.)
- [ ] `EntityType` registration
- [ ] Renderer and model classes loaded only on the physical client
- [ ] Register the renderer with `EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterRenderers` (NeoForge)
      or `EntityRendererRegistry` (Fabric); register model layers separately
- [ ] Spawn egg item (optional)
- [ ] Spawn rules / biome modifier

name: test
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@d0cc045d04ccac9d8b7881df0226f9e82c39688e # v6.8.0
      # ffmpeg is only for test_compile_small_edl. Without recommends apt skips mesa, VA/VDPAU drivers and
      # pocketsphinx-en-us (about half the download), and with man-db's auto-update off dpkg skips the man-page
      # reindex that can take minutes on the runner. When the Ubuntu mirror crawls (it has, at ~150 KB/s), the step
      # gives up after 8 minutes and the run goes on: that one test skips without ffmpeg instead of failing the build.
      - name: ffmpeg
        timeout-minutes: 8
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          sudo rm -f /var/lib/man-db/auto-update
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ffmpeg
      - run: uv run --with pytest pytest -q tests
      - run: ./bin/um --help && for g in scan fal comfy sprixen voidless sprite render3d video win backup publish kb fas
      - name: knowledge base
        run: ./bin/um kb check --index
      - name: nothing that shouldn't ship
        run: ./bin/um publish check .

305	`find-class` accepts either an `artifactId` or the shared object `target` shape. For a workspace-relative dependency, pass `target: { kind: "dependency", group, name, versionFromProject: true }` with top-level `projectPath`. Fabric-style umbrella JARs are searched through their nested `.class` inventories; a top-level class match can then be passed to `get-class-source` or `get-class-members`, which resolve the containing nested JAR. Dotted inner-class matches are also readable through `get-class-source`. An empty result means no match in the class inventories that could be read: a nested JAR that cannot be read or exceeds the nested-entry size cap is skipped without a warning, and when the artifact's source coverage excludes `net.minecraft` and the query is a Minecraft-style class name, `warnings` says so and `suggestedCall` points to `get-class-source`.
306	
307	For indexed source matches, a qualified name is checked against the full enclosing-type chain in that file and returned in the requested spelling; same-named types in other indexed files do not substitute for a missing type.
308	
309	For unobfuscated releases such as `26.1+`, `obfuscated` names the runtime jar's names as shipped, which are already Mojang names: both `obfuscated` and `mojang` are accepted, a namespace field that would report `obfuscated` (`mappingApplied`, `returnedNamespace`, and the other reported namespace fields) reports `mojang` instead, and `provenance.unobfuscatedRuntime: true` marks the artifact. `requestedMapping` is not relabelled, so for an omitted or `obfuscated` request, `requestedMapping: "obfuscated"` next to `mappingApplied: "mojang"` is an identity, not a fallback. `mapping="mojang"` uses the runtime/decompile path directly and skips Loom source-jar discovery. When an artifact or class tool resolves a 26.1+ target with `intermediary` or `yarn`, it falls back to the runtime names with a warning and reports them as `mojang`; the lifecycle tools keep reporting the requested `intermediary` or `yarn`. An explicit `intermediary` or `yarn` sent with an already-resolved `artifactId` skips that fallback: `get-class-source` and `get-class-members` still report `mojang` in `mappingApplied`, but `get-class-members` and `batch-class-members` entries keep the requested name in `returnedNamespace`. This applies to version targets, Minecraft runtime coordinates, and JAR targets whose own contents (a top-level `version.json` with a 26.1+ `id`, `net/minecraft/SharedConstants.class`, and no `.java` sources) prove a 26.1+ Minecraft runtime jar; see [docs/tool-reference.md → Lookup Rules](docs/tool-reference.md#lookup-rules). Dependency jars whose own version only looks like `26.x` keep `obfuscated`. `manage-cache` metadata and the access-widener/access-transformer validation provenance also keep `obfuscated`; see [docs/tool-reference.md → Namespace Definitions](docs/tool-reference.md#namespace-definitions).

19	---
20	# Minecraft 26.2 NeoForge modpack audit: diagnostics mod, javac builds, zombie-process and config-loop root causes, measured perf mods
21	
22	Audited a 100-mod NeoForge 26.2 pack, built an observe-only diagnostics mod (metrics, sampling profiler, event
23	monitor, inspectors, benchmark) and a small fix mod, both compiled with plain javac, and verified everything in
24	the real client via a scripted lab instance (autobench + in-game screenshots, no OS input). Then A/B-tested the
25	usual performance mods per mod and per scene; only two of four gave a measurable gain.
26	
27	## Setup
28	- Ownership: Minecraft: Java Edition through Xbox Game Pass (Java & Bedrock Edition for PC) on the author's
29	  Microsoft account. The two offline clients in Gotcha 30 were lab test clients of that owned copy, started by
30	  scripts on the same machine.
31	- TLauncher instance (`versions/<name>` is the gameDir), NeoForge 26.2.0.88 universal + patched client jar in
32	  `libraries/net/neoforged/...`; game runtime = Mojang `java-runtime-epsilon` (Java 25).
33	- Build JDK: any JDK 25. No Gradle needed.
34	
35	## Route and why
36	Minecraft 26.x ships **unobfuscated**, so mods compile directly against
37	`minecraft-client-patched-<ver>.jar` + `neoforge-<ver>-universal.jar` + the libraries listed in the version json.
38	No remapping, no refmap. A tiny Python script builds the classpath from the version json and a UTF-8 javac
39	`@argfile` (needed when paths contain non-ASCII characters).
40	Related: [Fabric mods for Minecraft 26.x](../../techniques/fabric-mod-for-26-x-without-mappings.md) (the Fabric side
41	of the same unobfuscated toolchain) and
42	[testing a mod inside a large modpack, headless](../../techniques/testing-a-fabric-mod-inside-a-large-modpack-headless.md).
43	
44	## How the game works (what we had to learn)
45	- GUI in 26.2: screens draw in `extractRenderState(GuiGraphicsExtractor, mx, my, pt)`; open via
46	  `mc.gui.setScreen()` / read `mc.gui.screen()`; HUD hidden flag = `mc.gui.hud.isHidden()`.
47	  HUD elements from other mods can end up above a screen's content; call `g.nextStratum()` before drawing.
48	- Keys: `KeyMapping(name, IKeyConflictContext, InputConstants.Type, code, KeyMapping.Category)`; categories are
49	  records registered via `RegisterKeyMappingsEvent.registerCategory`.
50	- Event bus 8.0.5: a listener added with `receiveCanceled=false` (the default) skips events an earlier listener
51	  cancelled, so use `receiveCanceled=true` for timing hooks. The bus drops that check for event classes that don't
52	  implement `ICancellableEvent` (`ListenerList` unwraps the filter), so the ClassCastException we saw with
53	  `receiveCanceled=false` on a non-cancellable event has some other cause; not resolved.
54	- Timing all listeners of an event = HIGHEST listener stores start, LOWEST(receiveCanceled) listener stores end.
55	- NeoForge `TimeTracker` (entity/BE) is shared between client and server threads -> racy in singleplayer; use own
56	  mixins on `ServerLevel#tickNonPassenger` and the `BlockEntityTicker#tick` call in
57	  `LevelChunk$BoundTickingBlockEntity#tick`.
58	- Stack frames carry the JPMS module name (= mod id for most mods); mixin handlers carry `$modid$` in the method
59	  name (`handler$abc000$modid$name`) -> per-mod attribution for a sampling profiler.
60	- `FramerateLimitTracker`: with `inactivityFpsLimit:"afk"` FPS is capped at 30 after 60 s without input. Any
61	  unattended benchmark must disable it or record the throttle reason.
62	- Client exit: `Main` ends but the JVM stays alive if any mod left a non-daemon thread.
63	
64	## Build steps
65	1. Classpath from version json (libraries with os rules for windows) + patched client + NeoForge universal.
66	2. `javac --release 25 -proc:none @args`, copy resources (`META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml`, mixin json, lang),
67	   `jar --create` with `Automatic-Module-Name`.
68	3. Mixin config: `"required": false`, `"defaultRequire": 0`, `@Pseudo` + `remap=false` for targets in other mods.
69	
70	## Verification
71	- Lab copy of the instance launched with the same JVM args as the launcher, `--quickPlaySingleplayer`, and
72	  system properties driving an in-mod autobench (warmup, 60 s run, snapshot, quit) and an in-mod UI self-test
73	  (opens each tab, saves `Screenshot.grab` PNGs). Results read from JSON reports + `latest.log`.
74	- Root causes proven by A/B: process exit time (never exits by itself 6/6 without fix, killed after 35-90 s;
75	  exits in 1-3 s 7/7 with fix); config rewrite loop reproduced by running two instances with a shared config
76	  dir, gone with the fix.
77	- Behaviour of a patched machine mod checked without trusting mod code: a setup command file fills one machine
78	  of each kind with raw food + fuel, and after the run a ~100-line Anvil/NBT reader dumps their saved `Items` from
79	  `dimensions/minecraft/overworld/region/*.mca` (26.x world layout); with/without the fix must be identical.
80	
81	## Performance mods on 26.2 (measured in this pack, 60 s runs, 8 GB heap, laptop i5-10200H + RTX 3060)
82	Base noise between two identical runs: MSPT ~1.5%, FPS ~1% standing; FPS ~8% in the crowd scene.
83	- Lithium 0.25.3 (NeoForge): server MSPT 20.7 -> 15.0-15.5 ms (-25..28%), worst second -30%, same in the
84	  crowd scene. 98 `@Overwrite`s, no conflict with ~100 other mods; machine/block-entity behaviour identical
85	  in the saved-world A/B dump. Kept.
86	- EntityCulling 1.11.3: standing in a field -> no change; sealed stone box 20 blocks ahead with 169 chests +
87	  338 NoAI mobs -> FPS 36-39 -> 47-51 (+22..36%), frame p99 -20%. Logs a harmless "refmap could not be read"
88	  (26.x is unobfuscated). Its licence (tr7zw Protective License) allows it in CurseForge- and Modrinth-hosted packs
89	  and no other redistribution of the jar, so a pack you zip up yourself can't carry it. Kept.
90	- FerriteCore 9.0.0 (Modrinth lists it for 26.1-26.1.2): live heap after full GC 1766 -> 1725 MiB (-2.5%);
91	  most of its old savings seem to be in vanilla by now. FPS -3% in 2 of 3 runs (noise level). Both it and
92	  Lithium `@Overwrite` `PalettedContainer.acquire/release`; no error or conflict warning in the log.
93	  Not kept: no real benefit.
94	- ImmediatelyFast 1.16.5: no effect beyond noise standing, in the crowd scene, or with the inventory + JEI item
95	  list open (+2% FPS). Not kept.
96	- World generation (spectator route, 24 blocks/s): two identical base runs differed x2.9 in MSPT, so no
97	  difference from any of these mods can be claimed.
98	
99	2026-10-12 additions (same lab, interleaved, 2-3 repeats):
100	- C2ME (c2me-neoforge 0.4.2-alpha.0.98): spectator flight 24 blocks/s, new chunks/s 4.5-4.9 -> 9.2-10.9 in a
101	  Terralith all_skylands world (TPS 10 -> 17-19), Twilight Forest 13-16 -> 43, a custom sphere world 13.5 -> 28-30.
102	  FPS -4..-19% during that flight (client meshes more chunks). Terrain identical to vanilla; feature placement
103	  (trees, ore blobs, ice) differs between ANY two runs, vanilla included (neighbour-chunk generation order), and two
104	  C2ME runs differ from each other as much as from vanilla. Kept.
105	- Fast Noise 1.0.40: no effect alone or with C2ME. Moonrise 1.1.2: crashes at registration with Adorn (custom
106	  `Property` subclass lacks `moonrise$getIdFor`). ModernFix-mVUS 5.27.21: no startup gain here, and its
107	  "missing perf mods" warning screen blocks unattended launches (`mixin.feature.warn_missing_perf_mods=false`).
108	  Ksyxis: world join -1 s but stops keeping spawn chunks loaded.
109	- Quick Pack 1.5.1: boot to world 69.5 -> 53.4 s with a 20 MB zip resource pack (it speeds up zip pack listing). Kept.
110	- Get It Together Drops 1.5 + Clumps 26.2.1: 1178 dropped items + 600 XP orbs: entities 2150 -> 1230, FPS +19%,
111	  MSPT -20%. Kept.
112	- GC (Java 25, 8 GB, 4-core laptop): G1 and generational ZGC tie on mean FPS/MSPT; G1 uses half the heap
113	  (3.5-5 vs 7-7.8 GB) but frame p99 +4-6 ms and 60-100 ms max frames; ZGC kept. A first single round looked like a
114	  G1 win: repeat GC comparisons.
115	
116	## Gotchas
117	1. When launched from a sandboxed agent shell on Windows, `HttpClient`/`Selector` creation can fail with
118	   "Unable to establish loopback connection" (AF_UNIX in TEMP). Fix for lab runs:
119	   `-Djdk.net.unixdomain.tmpdir=%PUBLIC%\<dir>` (a short ASCII path). Collective's update checker crashes mod construction otherwise.
120	2. Immersive Melodies 0.8.0 starts its MIDI poller as a non-daemon endless thread and opens Java's software
121	   sequencer (another non-daemon thread) -> `javaw.exe` never exits after closing the game.
122	3. Balm 26.2.0.9 enum/validated config values: validator accepts `null`, so missing keys are never written but
123	   their comments are "corrected" on every check. One instance: one rewrite. Two instances sharing `config/`:
124	   endless ping-pong via both FileWatchers (~2 writes/s) and eventually `WritingException REPLACE_ATOMIC`.
125	   Gotcha 2 + 3 together explain "the pack starts twice and then crashes on a config file".
126	4. A huge `-Xmx` with ZGC on a laptop: the heap grows to ~15 GB before a cycle; when the OS runs out of RAM the
127	   game stalls for seconds (MSPT 500 ms). 8 GB (live set after a full GC ~1.8 GB) removed the stalls.
128	5. Several mods ship pre-26.x data (item predicates `{"item":..}`, ingredient objects, recipe category "tools");
129	   26.2 rejects them at load. A small local data-pack mod with corrected copies (ordering AFTER) restores them; the
130	   copies are those mods' own data, so share such a pack only where their licences allow.
131	6. Bash heredocs from the agent tool can mangle backslashes in Python/Java snippets; write such files with the
132	   editor tool instead.
133	7. TLauncher memory: it takes the version json's `default_user_jvm` args, drops their `-Xmx` and appends its own
134	   `-Xmx<minecraft.memory.ram3>` last, so a heap limit cannot be pinned in the version json. A
135	   `-XX:SoftMaxHeapSize` there is worse: if the slider is ever set below it the JVM refuses to start. Set
136	   `minecraft.memory.ram3` in `%APPDATA%\.tlauncher\tlauncher-2.0.properties` while TLauncher is closed (it
137	   rewrites the file on exit) and keep the CRLF line endings.
138	8. `jcmd <pid> GC.class_histogram` (live-set measurement) stops the whole JVM for ~2 s on an 8 GB ZGC heap. The
139	   server logs it as "Can't keep up! ... 2xxx ms"; check those timestamps against the benchmark window. One of our
140	   runs had it land inside the window and looked like a -97% regression until it was rerun.
141	9. Standing-still benchmarks cannot show render-side mods. Use scenes: an open inventory with JEI's item list
142	   (GUI batching) and a sealed box of mobs + chests in view (occlusion culling).
143	10. Twilight Forest re26 4.8.4208 JEI plugin dies on the first call: `RecipeViewerConstants.getAllUncraftingRecipes`
144	   calls `assemble(CraftingInput.EMPTY)` on every crafting recipe and vanilla `DecoratedPotRecipe` (also
145	   `ImbueRecipe`, Crop Critters' `SeedBallRecipe`) throws AIOOBE on an empty grid, so every TF JEI category stays
146	   empty. Redirecting that call to "exception -> empty stack" restores the plugin; its uncrafting category then hits
147	   26.2's "Ingredients can't be empty" for cells whose items are all filtered out (59 recipes) - return null from
148	   the cell lambda and skip `add(null)`. Cost: TF's own recipe registration, JEI start 6.2 -> 7.9 s at world join.
149	11. Twilight Forest `EntityEvents.gatherPotentialSpawns` runs on every natural-spawn attempt in every dimension
150	   (thousands of calls per tick with ~2 300 chunks loaded) and its 64-entry cache is keyed by chunk x/z only (no
151	   dimension; thrashes). Remembering per StructureManager the chunks with no `ControlledSpawns` structure is exact
152	   (final once a chunk can tick, holds no StructureStart objects); compute chunks with TF structures fresh so the
153	   mutable "conquered" state never goes stale. A lab self-check mode recomputed 11.8 M overworld + 1.2 M TF-dimension
154	   answers: 0 mismatches. Effect: TF's share of server-thread samples halved, but MSPT only 15.5 -> 14.9 ms (-4%,
155	   ABAB without profiler). A profiled pair had shown -12.6%: the sampler inflates hot-call costs, so confirm
156	   gains with interleaved unprofiled runs.
157	12. Twilight Forest re26 port: `sounds.json` references 92 .ogg files the jar lacks (beetles, helmet crab, penguin,
158	   squirrel, troll, jar, candelabra, scepters). Upstream github.com/TeamTwilight/twilightforest (branch `latest`)
159	   has them unchanged under `src/main/resources/assets/twilightforest/sounds/`, but TF's README makes its sounds and
160	   structures All Rights Reserved (the other non-code assets are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), so they can't go into a resource
161	   jar you share. Report the missing files to the port's author.
162	13. JEI 30.x moved output computation into `SmithingCategoryExtension.setOutput`, which uses JEI's platform
163	   `RecipeHelper` (vanilla transform/trim only). Mods whose smithing extension subclasses that internal class
164	   without overriding `setOutput` (TF's NoTemplateSmithingExtension) now fail with "Unknown recipe type"; a mixin
165	   can add the missing `setOutput` with the erased signature `(SmithingRecipe, IIngredientAcceptor)`.
166	   26.2 also forbids `Ingredient.getValues()` on NeoForge custom ingredients - use `display().resolveForStacks`.
167	14. NeoForge 26.2 loads every file in `data/*/loot_modifiers/` as a modifier; the old
168	   `neoforge:loot_modifiers/global_loot_modifiers.json` list ({"replace","entries"}) is obsolete and logs
169	   "No key type". Mods' own modifiers still work; overriding the list with a no-op `neoforge:add_table` silences it.
170	15. Better Village 4.0.0 (26.2) ships a corrupted `desert_meeting_point_3.nbt` (gzip CRC error); the vanilla file
171	   from your own game jar is a drop-in replacement.
172	   2026-10-12: three more pieces in the same jar are corrupt (plains_small_house_4, savanna_small_house_6,
173	   snowy/streets/corner_03) - see gotcha 28.
174	16. Twilight Forest re26 4.8.4208, slow chunk loading in the TF dimension: its biome layer stack (`LazyArea` in front
175	   of each pure layer function) caches in a `ConcurrentHashMap` and evicts through a `LinkedBlockingQueue` locked on
176	   every miss, so all worldgen threads queue on one lock (profile: 95% of worker time in `LazyArea.getBiome`). A
177	   lock-free direct-mapped table of immutable (key, biome) entries (>= 8192 slots, THE_VOID not cached, as upstream)
178	   gives the same biomes (every pixel is a function of seed + x/z). Interleaved spectator flights, 90 s: new chunks/s
179	   4.0-4.3 -> 9.4-10.7, TPS 8.9 -> 17.6-18.5. A self-check that recomputes cache hits must not re-verify nested layers
180	   (ThreadLocal guard) or it grows exponentially; with the guard: 4.35e9 lookups, 0 mismatches.
181	17. OptiFine CTM resource packs (here Excalibur V26.3_01, whose `optifine/ctm/_transitions` overlays are
182	   pixel-identical to its 1.12 version) render on NeoForge 26.2 + Sodium 0.9.1 with Continuity 3.0.7+26.2 - but
183	   every chunk containing an overlay with `tintIndex=0` + `tintBlock=snow` failed to mesh and the client crashed: 26.2
184	   `BlockColors.getTintSource(state, index)` returns null when the block has no tint layer, Continuity's
185	   `RenderUtil.getTintColor` dereferences it. A HEAD mixin returning -1 (untinted, what OptiFine does) fixes it.
186	   Sources: both from CurseForge. Continuity 3.0.7+26.2 is "Continuity: NeoForged", aspctt's NeoForge port
187	   (project 1679396, file 8960914; also on Modrinth as `continuity-neoforged`, source
188	   github.com/aspctt/continuity-neoforge, whose 26.1+ branch calls `getTintSource(...).colorInWorld(...)` with no
189	   null check), not PepperCode1's Continuity. Excalibur V26.3_01 is file 8948603 of project 326818.
190	   Continuity (like OptiFine) loads CTM `.properties` from ALL packs: a same-path file in a higher pack does not
191	   replace the lower one, both rules run. Cost of the transitions here: -11% FPS (interleaved runs).
192	18. 26.2 mipmaps: one block sprite whose side is not a multiple of 16 caps the whole block atlas
193	   ("dropping miplevel from 4 to 0"); the log only names the sprites at each step down, so scan all
194	   `textures/block/**` PNG headers (+ `.mcmeta` frame size). Here 32 sprites in 4 furniture/food mods. Integer
195	   nearest-neighbour upscales look identical on models (UVs are fractions); large renders resampled by <2%. Expect the
196	   atlas to grow anyway: 26.2 `Stitcher` pads every sprite by `1 << mipLevel` on each side (16x16 -> 48x48), so 4875
197	   block sprites went 4096x2048 (mip 0) -> 8192x4096 (mip 4), ~+140 MB VRAM, +7 s to the menu, FPS unchanged, p99 -15%.
198	19. Porting 1.21.1 and 26.1 mods to 26.2 (YUNG's API 6.1.3 for 26.1.2; Ribbits 4.1.4 and NeoBiosphere 1.0.6 for
199	   1.21.1; javac only): `ResourceLocation` -> `Identifier`; `StructureProcessor` is an interface: `codec()` replaces
200	   `getType()`, the `STRUCTURE_PROCESSOR` registry holds MapCodecs (no `StructureProcessorType<T>`), and
201	   `StructureTemplate` calls `process(level, pos, refPos, original, processed, settings, template)` - the old
202	   `processBlock` arguments plus the template, so bodies port unchanged; `EntityType.X` constants moved to
203	   `EntityTypes`; entity `immuneTo` is a block tag; `FriendlyByteBuf.read/writeIdentifier`;
204	   `SpawnEggItem.getType(ItemStack)` is static and reads `DataComponents.ENTITY_DATA` (use
205	   `Item.Properties.spawnEgg(type)`; ENTITY_TYPE registers before ITEM); `Level.getDayTime()` ->
206	   `getOverworldClockTime()`; `FireBlock.setFlammable` is private again (use an `@Invoker`); `ItemBlockRenderTypes`
207	   is gone (the chunk layer comes from sprite transparency); `RenderTypes.entityCutout` has cull off (= old
208	   `entityCutoutNoCull`); `ItemInHandRenderer.renderArmWithItem` -> `submitArmWithItem`.
209	   GeckoLib 5.5 for 26.2 moved to package `com.geckolib`; per-frame bone visibility goes through
210	   `GeoRenderer.adjustModelBonesForRender(RenderPassInfo, BoneSnapshots)` + `BoneSnapshot.skipRender/skipChildrenRender`
211	   instead of mutating shared `GeoBone`s.
212	20. 26.2 data: the `minecraft:random_patch` feature type is gone ("Unknown registry key ... minecraft:random_patch",
213	   the whole registry load fails). Vanilla moved patches into placed-feature modifiers; convert
214	   tries/xz_spread/y_spread to `count` + `random_offset` with `trapezoid(-s..s, plateau 0)` (old offset was
215	   `nextInt(s+1) - nextInt(s+1)`) + the inner feature's filters; the configured feature becomes the inner feature.
216	21. Mixins targeting lambdas break silently: YUNG's API raises the jigsaw pool weight cap with a `@WrapOperation` on
217	   `lambda$static$1`, but in 26.2 the `Codec.intRange(1, 150)` call sits in `lambda$static$0`; with `require = 0`
218	   nothing applies and pools with weights > 150 fail later. A static check of every mixin's target class, method
219	   names, `@Shadow`/`@Accessor`/`@Invoker` names and `@At(target)` owners via `javap -p` caught it (and the
220	   renamed `ItemInHandRenderer` method) before any lab run.
221	22. Overworld-replacing generator (NeoBiosphere-style spheres) without touching other worlds: register a
222	   `NoiseBasedChunkGenerator` subclass + a world preset; build its settings at `ChunkMap.<init>` (the only
223	   `generatorSettings()` call that creates the `RandomState`) with `finalDensity` wrapped in
224	   `rangeChoice(sphereDistance, 0, 1, original, -1e6)`; gate every other mixin (aquifer, heightmap, biome source) on
225	   "this level's generator is the sphere generator". Biomes/structures of the pack (Terralith) then appear inside.
226	23. Cube Animals 2.1b: `CrocodileLeaveWaterGoal.findLandTarget` (from `canUse`, every 2 ticks per crocodile in water)
227	   walks radii 2..16 but rescans the whole (2r+1)^2 square each radius: ~36 000 columns x 6 heights x ~12 block reads
228	   when there is no land. 52 crocodiles in a swamp lab world: 86% of the server thread, TPS ~8. Same scan skipping
229	   already-checked inner squares (identical result) + a 10-tick retry after a miss: crocodiles 110 -> 3 ms/tick,
230	   TPS 20 (self-check vs the original loop: 0 mismatches).
231	24. Biome-gated content vs world presets: Terralith's `all_skylands` preset uses only 4 `skylands_*` biomes, so
232	   swamp-only structures (Ribbits villages) never generate there. Check the preset's biome list before promising
233	   content in an existing world.
234	25. Lab screenshots: `Graphics.CopyFromScreen` of the game window's rectangle captures whatever window is on top;
235	   `PrintWindow(hwnd, hdc, PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)` grabs the GL window's own content without stealing focus.
236	   A user's screen-share/stream running in the background shifts FPS between sessions by 15-20%: compare FPS only
237	   inside one interleaved series.
238	26. Twilight Forest re26 hooks `Level.isRainingAt` in every dimension: in clear weather it walks 32 blocks up per call
239	   looking for its cloud blocks; dropped items/XP/mobs call it every tick (12% of the server thread with 2000 items).
240	   Check the chunk sections' palettes (`maybeHas(CloudBlock)`) first; verified 7M calls, 0 mismatches.
241	27. Twilight Forest re26 JEI plugin calls `Objects.requireNonNull(Minecraft.getSingleplayerServer())` -> NPE on any
242	   client that joined a LAN/remote world: no TF categories in JEI there. Feed it a `RecipeManager` filled from JEI's
243	   synced recipes (`mezz.jei.common.Internal.getClientSyncedRecipes()`) and have the host
244	   `OnDatapackSyncEvent.sendRecipes(...)` TF's uncrafting and drying types.
245	28. Better Village 4.0.0 ships FOUR corrupt `.nbt` pieces (desert_meeting_point_3, plains_small_house_4,
246	   savanna_small_house_6, snowy/streets/corner_03): gzip CRC errors and invalid NBT. `StructureTemplateManager`
247	   caches the failed load as empty until restart, so villages lose those houses. Copy the vanilla pieces from your
248	   own game jar into a local data pack at the same paths (they're Mojang's files: don't publish them) and report
249	   the corrupt files to Better Village. Scan every `.nbt` of every jar (1168 here) with a plain gzip+NBT parser;
250	   only these 4 were bad.
251	29. "Detected unsafe terrain read during worldgen ... step: minecraft:spawn" (vanilla logs one line, no stack):
252	   ~370k lines / 90 MB log per 40 min in a normal world. A mixin at `WorldGenRegion.warnIfReadOutsideWriteZone`'s
253	   log call that prints a stack for the first N cases named Naturalist 2.0.5 `Hippo.checkHippoSpawnRules`
254	   (33x3x33 water scan, `hasChunk` true for the region's neighbours). Treat only the centre chunk as loaded when the
255	   level is a `WorldGenRegion`.
256	30. In 26.2 the integrated server starts with `setUsesAuthentication(true)`: two offline lab clients cannot share a
257	   LAN world unless the lab build turns it off (lab only; normal LAN play keeps authentication on). Start the second
258	   client ~4 min earlier than you think: two clients on one machine boot slowly.
259	31. `/locate` (and anything using `findNearestMapStructure`) for a structure that cannot exist in the world (villages
260	   in Terralith all_skylands) froze the server 148 s.
261	32. TLauncher modpack folders carry `TLauncherAdditional.json` with URLs for the NeoForge libraries (incl. the patched
262	   client); `versions/<id>/<id>.jar` is byte-identical to Mojang's client.jar, which the launcher downloads from
263	   `downloads.client`. Don't hand the version folder around as a zip: besides Mojang's jar it holds every mod's jar,
264	   and many licences (EntityCulling's; Balm and Better Village are All Rights Reserved) don't allow re-hosting them.
265	   Share a mod list, or a CurseForge/Modrinth pack that downloads each mod from its own page.
266	33. Showcase filming: gfxcapture timestamps are wall-clock and fine; empty-sky takes came from starting camera moves
267	   before chunks existed. Pregenerate a dedicated "film world" (visit start/middle/end of every path, wait until all
268	   chunks within 7 of the CAMERA are on the client, save), then film from copies. Sodium's
269	   `isTerrainRenderComplete()` flickers and is useless as a readiness signal.
270	34. Move the camera every rendered frame with `LocalPlayer.snapTo(x,y,z,yaw,pitch)` plus `xOld/yOld/zOld` and head
271	   rotation from `RenderFrameEvent.Pre`: smooth paths, no tick interpolation steps. Cancel `ToastManager.addToast`
272	   while filming.
273	35. `um video compile` with Cyrillic titles: Space Grotesk (the default title font) has no Cyrillic, and older `um`
274	   read the EDL with the locale encoding (we ran it with `PYTHONUTF8=1` and swapped the font paths in a small
275	   wrapper). Fixed in `um` since (#259): EDLs are read as UTF-8, and the EDL theme's `title_font` / `body_font` /
276	   `mono_font` take .ttf paths, so point them at a font with Cyrillic (Segoe UI, Constantia).
277	36. Minecraft music OGGs sit in `assets/objects/<hash>` (index `assets/indexes/<id>.json`, key
278	   `minecraft/sounds/music/game/...`); `playsound ... master` of a music event did not end up in a process-loopback
279	   recording.
280	37. NeoBiosphere-style worlds: spheres radius 128, centres every 500 blocks at y 62 - orbit at ~235 blocks with render
281	   distance 20 to show a whole sphere.
282

# Minecraft 26.2 NeoForge modpack audit: diagnostics mod, javac builds, zombie-process and config-loop root causes, measured perf mods

Audited a 100-mod NeoForge 26.2 pack, built an observe-only diagnostics mod (metrics, sampling profiler, event
monitor, inspectors, benchmark) and a small fix mod, both compiled with plain javac, and verified everything in
the real client via a scripted lab instance (autobench + in-game screenshots, no OS input). Then A/B-tested the
usual performance mods per mod and per scene; only two of four gave a measurable gain.

## Setup
- Ownership: Minecraft: Java Edition through Xbox Game Pass (Java & Bedrock Edition for PC) on the author's
  Microsoft account. The two offline clients in Gotcha 30 were lab test clients of that owned copy, started by
  scripts on the same machine.
- TLauncher instance (`versions/<name>` is the gameDir), NeoForge 26.2.0.88 universal + patched client jar in
  `libraries/net/neoforged/...`; game runtime = Mojang `java-runtime-epsilon` (Java 25).
- Build JDK: any JDK 25. No Gradle needed.

## Route and why
Minecraft 26.x ships **unobfuscated**, so mods compile directly against
`minecraft-client-patched-<ver>.jar` + `neoforge-<ver>-universal.jar` + the libraries listed in the version json.
No remapping, no refmap. A tiny Python script builds the classpath from the version json and a UTF-8 javac
`@argfile` (needed when paths contain non-ASCII characters).
Related: [Fabric mods for Minecraft 26.x](../../techniques/fabric-mod-for-26-x-without-mappings.md) (the Fabric side
of the same unobfuscated toolchain) and
[testing a mod inside a large modpack, headless](../../techniques/testing-a-fabric-mod-inside-a-large-modpack-headless.md).

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- GUI in 26.2: screens draw in `extractRenderState(GuiGraphicsExtractor, mx, my, pt)`; open via
  `mc.gui.setScreen()` / read `mc.gui.screen()`; HUD hidden flag = `mc.gui.hud.isHidden()`.
  HUD elements from other mods can end up above a screen's content; call `g.nextStratum()` before drawing.
- Keys: `KeyMapping(name, IKeyConflictContext, InputConstants.Type, code, KeyMapping.Category)`; categories are
  records registered via `RegisterKeyMappingsEvent.registerCategory`.
- Event bus 8.0.5: a listener added with `receiveCanceled=false` (the default) skips events an earlier listener
  cancelled, so use `receiveCanceled=true` for timing hooks. The bus drops that check for event classes that don't
  implement `ICancellableEvent` (`ListenerList` unwraps the filter), so the ClassCastException we saw with
  `receiveCanceled=false` on a non-cancellable event has some other cause; not resolved.
- Timing all listeners of an event = HIGHEST listener stores start, LOWEST(receiveCanceled) listener stores end.
- NeoForge `TimeTracker` (entity/BE) is shared between client and server threads -> racy in singleplayer; use own
  mixins on `ServerLevel#tickNonPassenger` and the `BlockEntityTicker#tick` call in
  `LevelChunk$BoundTickingBlockEntity#tick`.
- Stack frames carry the JPMS module name (= mod id for most mods); mixin handlers carry `$modid$` in the method
  name (`handler$abc000$modid$name`) -> per-mod attribution for a sampling profiler.
- `FramerateLimitTracker`: with `inactivityFpsLimit:"afk"` FPS is capped at 30 after 60 s without input. Any
  unattended benchmark must disable it or record the throttle reason.
- Client exit: `Main` ends but the JVM stays alive if any mod left a non-daemon thread.

## Build steps
1. Classpath from version json (libraries with os rules for windows) + patched client + NeoForge universal.
2. `javac --release 25 -proc:none @args`, copy resources (`META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml`, mixin json, lang),
   `jar --create` with `Automatic-Module-Name`.
3. Mixin config: `"required": false`, `"defaultRequire": 0`, `@Pseudo` + `remap=false` for targets in other mods.

## Verification
- Lab copy of the instance launched with the same JVM args as the launcher, `--quickPlaySingleplayer`, and
  system properties driving an in-mod autobench (warmup, 60 s run, snapshot, quit) and an in-mod UI self-test
  (opens each tab, saves `Screenshot.grab` PNGs). Results read from JSON reports + `latest.log`.
- Root causes proven by A/B: process exit time (never exits by itself 6/6 without fix, killed after 35-90 s;
  exits in 1-3 s 7/7 with fix); config rewrite loop reproduced by running two instances with a shared config
  dir, gone with the fix.
- Behaviour of a patched machine mod checked without trusting mod code: a setup command file fills one machine
  of each kind with raw food + fuel, and after the run a ~100-line Anvil/NBT reader dumps their saved `Items` from
  `dimensions/minecraft/overworld/region/*.mca` (26.x world layout); with/without the fix must be identical.

## Performance mods on 26.2 (measured in this pack, 60 s runs, 8 GB heap, laptop i5-10200H + RTX 3060)
Base noise between two identical runs: MSPT ~1.5%, FPS ~1% standing; FPS ~8% in the crowd scene.
- Lithium 0.25.3 (NeoForge): server MSPT 20.7 -> 15.0-15.5 ms (-25..28%), worst second -30%, same in the
  crowd scene. 98 `@Overwrite`s, no conflict with ~100 other mods; machine/block-entity behaviour identical
  in the saved-world A/B dump. Kept.
- EntityCulling 1.11.3: standing in a field -> no change; sealed stone box 20 blocks ahead with 169 chests +
  338 NoAI mobs -> FPS 36-39 -> 47-51 (+22..36%), frame p99 -20%. Logs a harmless "refmap could not be read"
  (26.x is unobfuscated). Its licence (tr7zw Protective License) allows it in CurseForge- and Modrinth-hosted packs
  and no other redistribution of the jar, so a pack you zip up yourself can't carry it. Kept.
- FerriteCore 9.0.0 (Modrinth lists it for 26.1-26.1.2): live heap after full GC 1766 -> 1725 MiB (-2.5%);
  most of its old savings seem to be in vanilla by now. FPS -3% in 2 of 3 runs (noise level). Both it and
  Lithium `@Overwrite` `PalettedContainer.acquire/release`; no error or conflict warning in the log.
  Not kept: no real benefit.
- ImmediatelyFast 1.16.5: no effect beyond noise standing, in the crowd scene, or with the inventory + JEI item
  list open (+2% FPS). Not kept.
- World generation (spectator route, 24 blocks/s): two identical base runs differed x2.9 in MSPT, so no
  difference from any of these mods can be claimed.

2026-10-12 additions (same lab, interleaved, 2-3 repeats):
- C2ME (c2me-neoforge 0.4.2-alpha.0.98): spectator flight 24 blocks/s, new chunks/s 4.5-4.9 -> 9.2-10.9 in a
  Terralith all_skylands world (TPS 10 -> 17-19), Twilight Forest 13-16 -> 43, a custom sphere world 13.5 -> 28-30.
  FPS -4..-19% during that flight (client meshes more chunks). Terrain identical to vanilla; feature placement
  (trees, ore blobs, ice) differs between ANY two runs, vanilla included (neighbour-chunk generation order), and two
  C2ME runs differ from each other as much as from vanilla. Kept.
- Fast Noise 1.0.40: no effect alone or with C2ME. Moonrise 1.1.2: crashes at registration with Adorn (custom
  `Property` subclass lacks `moonrise$getIdFor`). ModernFix-mVUS 5.27.21: no startup gain here, and its
  "missing perf mods" warning screen blocks unattended launches (`mixin.feature.warn_missing_perf_mods=false`).
  Ksyxis: world join -1 s but stops keeping spawn chunks loaded.
- Quick Pack 1.5.1: boot to world 69.5 -> 53.4 s with a 20 MB zip resource pack (it speeds up zip pack listing). Kept.
- Get It Together Drops 1.5 + Clumps 26.2.1: 1178 dropped items + 600 XP orbs: entities 2150 -> 1230, FPS +19%,
  MSPT -20%. Kept.
- GC (Java 25, 8 GB, 4-core laptop): G1 and generational ZGC tie on mean FPS/MSPT; G1 uses half the heap
  (3.5-5 vs 7-7.8 GB) but frame p99 +4-6 ms and 60-100 ms max frames; ZGC kept. A first single round looked like a
  G1 win: repeat GC comparisons.

## Gotchas
1. When launched from a sandboxed agent shell on Windows, `HttpClient`/`Selector` creation can fail with
   "Unable to establish loopback connection" (AF_UNIX in TEMP). Fix for lab runs:
   `-Djdk.net.unixdomain.tmpdir=%PUBLIC%\<dir>` (a short ASCII path). Collective's update checker crashes mod construction otherwise.
2. Immersive Melodies 0.8.0 starts its MIDI poller as a non-daemon endless thread and opens Java's software
   sequencer (another non-daemon thread) -> `javaw.exe` never exits after closing the game.
3. Balm 26.2.0.9 enum/validated config values: validator accepts `null`, so missing keys are never written but
   their comments are "corrected" on every check. One instance: one rewrite. Two instances sharing `config/`:
   endless ping-pong via both FileWatchers (~2 writes/s) and eventually `WritingException REPLACE_ATOMIC`.
   Gotcha 2 + 3 together explain "the pack starts twice and then crashes on a config file".
4. A huge `-Xmx` with ZGC on a laptop: the heap grows to ~15 GB before a cycle; when the OS runs out of RAM the
   game stalls for seconds (MSPT 500 ms). 8 GB (live set after a full GC ~1.8 GB) removed the stalls.
5. Several mods ship pre-26.x data (item predicates `{"item":..}`, ingredient objects, recipe category "tools");
   26.2 rejects them at load. A small local data-pack mod with corrected copies (ordering AFTER) restores them; the
   copies are those mods' own data, so share such a pack only where their licences allow.
6. Bash heredocs from the agent tool can mangle backslashes in Python/Java snippets; write such files with the
   editor tool instead.
7. TLauncher memory: it takes the version json's `default_user_jvm` args, drops their `-Xmx` and appends its own
   `-Xmx<minecraft.memory.ram3>` last, so a heap limit cannot be pinned in the version json. A
   `-XX:SoftMaxHeapSize` there is worse: if the slider is ever set below it the JVM refuses to start. Set
   `minecraft.memory.ram3` in `%APPDATA%\.tlauncher\tlauncher-2.0.properties` while TLauncher is closed (it
   rewrites the file on exit) and keep the CRLF line endings.
8. `jcmd <pid> GC.class_histogram` (live-set measurement) stops the whole JVM for ~2 s on an 8 GB ZGC heap. The
   server logs it as "Can't keep up! ... 2xxx ms"; check those timestamps against the benchmark window. One of our
   runs had it land inside the window and looked like a -97% regression until it was rerun.
9. Standing-still benchmarks cannot show render-side mods. Use scenes: an open inventory with JEI's item list
   (GUI batching) and a sealed box of mobs + chests in view (occlusion culling).
10. Twilight Forest re26 4.8.4208 JEI plugin dies on the first call: `RecipeViewerConstants.getAllUncraftingRecipes`
   calls `assemble(CraftingInput.EMPTY)` on every crafting recipe and vanilla `DecoratedPotRecipe` (also
   `ImbueRecipe`, Crop Critters' `SeedBallRecipe`) throws AIOOBE on an empty grid, so every TF JEI category stays
   empty. Redirecting that call to "exception -> empty stack" restores the plugin; its uncrafting category then hits
   26.2's "Ingredients can't be empty" for cells whose items are all filtered out (59 recipes) - return null from
   the cell lambda and skip `add(null)`. Cost: TF's own recipe registration, JEI start 6.2 -> 7.9 s at world join.
11. Twilight Forest `EntityEvents.gatherPotentialSpawns` runs on every natural-spawn attempt in every dimension
   (thousands of calls per tick with ~2 300 chunks loaded) and its 64-entry cache is keyed by chunk x/z only (no
   dimension; thrashes). Remembering per StructureManager the chunks with no `ControlledSpawns` structure is exact
   (final once a chunk can tick, holds no StructureStart objects); compute chunks with TF structures fresh so the
   mutable "conquered" state never goes stale. A lab self-check mode recomputed 11.8 M overworld + 1.2 M TF-dimension
   answers: 0 mismatches. Effect: TF's share of server-thread samples halved, but MSPT only 15.5 -> 14.9 ms (-4%,
   ABAB without profiler). A profiled pair had shown -12.6%: the sampler inflates hot-call costs, so confirm
   gains with interleaved unprofiled runs.
12. Twilight Forest re26 port: `sounds.json` references 92 .ogg files the jar lacks (beetles, helmet crab, penguin,
   squirrel, troll, jar, candelabra, scepters). Upstream github.com/TeamTwilight/twilightforest (branch `latest`)
   has them unchanged under `src/main/resources/assets/twilightforest/sounds/`, but TF's README makes its sounds and
   structures All Rights Reserved (the other non-code assets are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), so they can't go into a resource
   jar you share. Report the missing files to the port's author.
13. JEI 30.x moved output computation into `SmithingCategoryExtension.setOutput`, which uses JEI's platform
   `RecipeHelper` (vanilla transform/trim only). Mods whose smithing extension subclasses that internal class
   without overriding `setOutput` (TF's NoTemplateSmithingExtension) now fail with "Unknown recipe type"; a mixin
   can add the missing `setOutput` with the erased signature `(SmithingRecipe, IIngredientAcceptor)`.
   26.2 also forbids `Ingredient.getValues()` on NeoForge custom ingredients - use `display().resolveForStacks`.
14. NeoForge 26.2 loads every file in `data/*/loot_modifiers/` as a modifier; the old
   `neoforge:loot_modifiers/global_loot_modifiers.json` list ({"replace","entries"}) is obsolete and logs
   "No key type". Mods' own modifiers still work; overriding the list with a no-op `neoforge:add_table` silences it.
15. Better Village 4.0.0 (26.2) ships a corrupted `desert_meeting_point_3.nbt` (gzip CRC error); the vanilla file
   from your own game jar is a drop-in replacement.
   2026-10-12: three more pieces in the same jar are corrupt (plains_small_house_4, savanna_small_house_6,
   snowy/streets/corner_03) - see gotcha 28.
16. Twilight Forest re26 4.8.4208, slow chunk loading in the TF dimension: its biome layer stack (`LazyArea` in front
   of each pure layer function) caches in a `ConcurrentHashMap` and evicts through a `LinkedBlockingQueue` locked on
   every miss, so all worldgen threads queue on one lock (profile: 95% of worker time in `LazyArea.getBiome`). A
   lock-free direct-mapped table of immutable (key, biome) entries (>= 8192 slots, THE_VOID not cached, as upstream)
   gives the same biomes (every pixel is a function of seed + x/z). Interleaved spectator flights, 90 s: new chunks/s
   4.0-4.3 -> 9.4-10.7, TPS 8.9 -> 17.6-18.5. A self-check that recomputes cache hits must not re-verify nested layers
   (ThreadLocal guard) or it grows exponentially; with the guard: 4.35e9 lookups, 0 mismatches.
17. OptiFine CTM resource packs (here Excalibur V26.3_01, whose `optifine/ctm/_transitions` overlays are
   pixel-identical to its 1.12 version) render on NeoForge 26.2 + Sodium 0.9.1 with Continuity 3.0.7+26.2 - but
   every chunk containing an overlay with `tintIndex=0` + `tintBlock=snow` failed to mesh and the client crashed: 26.2
   `BlockColors.getTintSource(state, index)` returns null when the block has no tint layer, Continuity's
   `RenderUtil.getTintColor` dereferences it. A HEAD mixin returning -1 (untinted, what OptiFine does) fixes it.
   Sources: both from CurseForge. Continuity 3.0.7+26.2 is "Continuity: NeoForged", aspctt's NeoForge port
   (project 1679396, file 8960914; also on Modrinth as `continuity-neoforged`, source
   github.com/aspctt/continuity-neoforge, whose 26.1+ branch calls `getTintSource(...).colorInWorld(...)` with no
   null check), not PepperCode1's Continuity. Excalibur V26.3_01 is file 8948603 of project 326818.
   Continuity (like OptiFine) loads CTM `.properties` from ALL packs: a same-path file in a higher pack does not
   replace the lower one, both rules run. Cost of the transitions here: -11% FPS (interleaved runs).
18. 26.2 mipmaps: one block sprite whose side is not a multiple of 16 caps the whole block atlas
   ("dropping miplevel from 4 to 0"); the log only names the sprites at each step down, so scan all
   `textures/block/**` PNG headers (+ `.mcmeta` frame size). Here 32 sprites in 4 furniture/food mods. Integer
   nearest-neighbour upscales look identical on models (UVs are fractions); large renders resampled by <2%. Expect the
   atlas to grow anyway: 26.2 `Stitcher` pads every sprite by `1 << mipLevel` on each side (16x16 -> 48x48), so 4875
   block sprites went 4096x2048 (mip 0) -> 8192x4096 (mip 4), ~+140 MB VRAM, +7 s to the menu, FPS unchanged, p99 -15%.
19. Porting 1.21.1 and 26.1 mods to 26.2 (YUNG's API 6.1.3 for 26.1.2; Ribbits 4.1.4 and NeoBiosphere 1.0.6 for
   1.21.1; javac only): `ResourceLocation` -> `Identifier`; `StructureProcessor` is an interface: `codec()` replaces
   `getType()`, the `STRUCTURE_PROCESSOR` registry holds MapCodecs (no `StructureProcessorType<T>`), and
   `StructureTemplate` calls `process(level, pos, refPos, original, processed, settings, template)` - the old
   `processBlock` arguments plus the template, so bodies port unchanged; `EntityType.X` constants moved to
   `EntityTypes`; entity `immuneTo` is a block tag; `FriendlyByteBuf.read/writeIdentifier`;
   `SpawnEggItem.getType(ItemStack)` is static and reads `DataComponents.ENTITY_DATA` (use
   `Item.Properties.spawnEgg(type)`; ENTITY_TYPE registers before ITEM); `Level.getDayTime()` ->
   `getOverworldClockTime()`; `FireBlock.setFlammable` is private again (use an `@Invoker`); `ItemBlockRenderTypes`
   is gone (the chunk layer comes from sprite transparency); `RenderTypes.entityCutout` has cull off (= old
   `entityCutoutNoCull`); `ItemInHandRenderer.renderArmWithItem` -> `submitArmWithItem`.
   GeckoLib 5.5 for 26.2 moved to package `com.geckolib`; per-frame bone visibility goes through
   `GeoRenderer.adjustModelBonesForRender(RenderPassInfo, BoneSnapshots)` + `BoneSnapshot.skipRender/skipChildrenRender`
   instead of mutating shared `GeoBone`s.
20. 26.2 data: the `minecraft:random_patch` feature type is gone ("Unknown registry key ... minecraft:random_patch",
   the whole registry load fails). Vanilla moved patches into placed-feature modifiers; convert
   tries/xz_spread/y_spread to `count` + `random_offset` with `trapezoid(-s..s, plateau 0)` (old offset was
   `nextInt(s+1) - nextInt(s+1)`) + the inner feature's filters; the configured feature becomes the inner feature.
21. Mixins targeting lambdas break silently: YUNG's API raises the jigsaw pool weight cap with a `@WrapOperation` on
   `lambda$static$1`, but in 26.2 the `Codec.intRange(1, 150)` call sits in `lambda$static$0`; with `require = 0`
   nothing applies and pools with weights > 150 fail later. A static check of every mixin's target class, method
   names, `@Shadow`/`@Accessor`/`@Invoker` names and `@At(target)` owners via `javap -p` caught it (and the
   renamed `ItemInHandRenderer` method) before any lab run.
22. Overworld-replacing generator (NeoBiosphere-style spheres) without touching other worlds: register a
   `NoiseBasedChunkGenerator` subclass + a world preset; build its settings at `ChunkMap.<init>` (the only
   `generatorSettings()` call that creates the `RandomState`) with `finalDensity` wrapped in
   `rangeChoice(sphereDistance, 0, 1, original, -1e6)`; gate every other mixin (aquifer, heightmap, biome source) on
   "this level's generator is the sphere generator". Biomes/structures of the pack (Terralith) then appear inside.
23. Cube Animals 2.1b: `CrocodileLeaveWaterGoal.findLandTarget` (from `canUse`, every 2 ticks per crocodile in water)
   walks radii 2..16 but rescans the whole (2r+1)^2 square each radius: ~36 000 columns x 6 heights x ~12 block reads
   when there is no land. 52 crocodiles in a swamp lab world: 86% of the server thread, TPS ~8. Same scan skipping
   already-checked inner squares (identical result) + a 10-tick retry after a miss: crocodiles 110 -> 3 ms/tick,
   TPS 20 (self-check vs the original loop: 0 mismatches).
24. Biome-gated content vs world presets: Terralith's `all_skylands` preset uses only 4 `skylands_*` biomes, so
   swamp-only structures (Ribbits villages) never generate there. Check the preset's biome list before promising
   content in an existing world.
25. Lab screenshots: `Graphics.CopyFromScreen` of the game window's rectangle captures whatever window is on top;
   `PrintWindow(hwnd, hdc, PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)` grabs the GL window's own content without stealing focus.
   A user's screen-share/stream running in the background shifts FPS between sessions by 15-20%: compare FPS only
   inside one interleaved series.
26. Twilight Forest re26 hooks `Level.isRainingAt` in every dimension: in clear weather it walks 32 blocks up per call
   looking for its cloud blocks; dropped items/XP/mobs call it every tick (12% of the server thread with 2000 items).
   Check the chunk sections' palettes (`maybeHas(CloudBlock)`) first; verified 7M calls, 0 mismatches.
27. Twilight Forest re26 JEI plugin calls `Objects.requireNonNull(Minecraft.getSingleplayerServer())` -> NPE on any
   client that joined a LAN/remote world: no TF categories in JEI there. Feed it a `RecipeManager` filled from JEI's
   synced recipes (`mezz.jei.common.Internal.getClientSyncedRecipes()`) and have the host
   `OnDatapackSyncEvent.sendRecipes(...)` TF's uncrafting and drying types.
28. Better Village 4.0.0 ships FOUR corrupt `.nbt` pieces (desert_meeting_point_3, plains_small_house_4,
   savanna_small_house_6, snowy/streets/corner_03): gzip CRC errors and invalid NBT. `StructureTemplateManager`
   caches the failed load as empty until restart, so villages lose those houses. Copy the vanilla pieces from your
   own game jar into a local data pack at the same paths (they're Mojang's files: don't publish them) and report
   the corrupt files to Better Village. Scan every `.nbt` of every jar (1168 here) with a plain gzip+NBT parser;
   only these 4 were bad.
29. "Detected unsafe terrain read during worldgen ... step: minecraft:spawn" (vanilla logs one line, no stack):
   ~370k lines / 90 MB log per 40 min in a normal world. A mixin at `WorldGenRegion.warnIfReadOutsideWriteZone`'s
   log call that prints a stack for the first N cases named Naturalist 2.0.5 `Hippo.checkHippoSpawnRules`
   (33x3x33 water scan, `hasChunk` true for the region's neighbours). Treat only the centre chunk as loaded when the
   level is a `WorldGenRegion`.
30. In 26.2 the integrated server starts with `setUsesAuthentication(true)`: two offline lab clients cannot share a
   LAN world unless the lab build turns it off (lab only; normal LAN play keeps authentication on). Start the second
   client ~4 min earlier than you think: two clients on one machine boot slowly.
31. `/locate` (and anything using `findNearestMapStructure`) for a structure that cannot exist in the world (villages
   in Terralith all_skylands) froze the server 148 s.
32. TLauncher modpack folders carry `TLauncherAdditional.json` with URLs for the NeoForge libraries (incl. the patched
   client); `versions/<id>/<id>.jar` is byte-identical to Mojang's client.jar, which the launcher downloads from
   `downloads.client`. Don't hand the version folder around as a zip: besides Mojang's jar it holds every mod's jar,
   and many licences (EntityCulling's; Balm and Better Village are All Rights Reserved) don't allow re-hosting them.
   Share a mod list, or a CurseForge/Modrinth pack that downloads each mod from its own page.
33. Showcase filming: gfxcapture timestamps are wall-clock and fine; empty-sky takes came from starting camera moves
   before chunks existed. Pregenerate a dedicated "film world" (visit start/middle/end of every path, wait until all
   chunks within 7 of the CAMERA are on the client, save), then film from copies. Sodium's
   `isTerrainRenderComplete()` flickers and is useless as a readiness signal.
34. Move the camera every rendered frame with `LocalPlayer.snapTo(x,y,z,yaw,pitch)` plus `xOld/yOld/zOld` and head
   rotation from `RenderFrameEvent.Pre`: smooth paths, no tick interpolation steps. Cancel `ToastManager.addToast`
   while filming.
35. `um video compile` with Cyrillic titles: Space Grotesk (the default title font) has no Cyrillic, and older `um`
   read the EDL with the locale encoding (we ran it with `PYTHONUTF8=1` and swapped the font paths in a small
   wrapper). Fixed in `um` since (#259): EDLs are read as UTF-8, and the EDL theme's `title_font` / `body_font` /
   `mono_font` take .ttf paths, so point them at a font with Cyrillic (Segoe UI, Constantia).
36. Minecraft music OGGs sit in `assets/objects/<hash>` (index `assets/indexes/<id>.json`, key
   `minecraft/sounds/music/game/...`); `playsound ... master` of a music event did not end up in a process-loopback
   recording.
37. NeoBiosphere-style worlds: spheres radius 128, centres every 500 blocks at y 62 - orbit at ~235 blocks with render
   distance 20 to show a whole sphere.

# NeoForge 1.21.1 GameTests for mob AI: real survival players, structure y-offset, tick-0 hurt trap

> Testing custom-mob AI (warn/aggro/flee/feed goals) with Minecraft GameTests is
> mostly fighting the *harness*, not the mob. Four non-obvious environment quirks
> make every entity-AI test silently fail if you don't know them.

## When to use it

Any NeoForge/Forge GameTest that needs a mob to perceive or attack a player —
`runGameTestServer` on MC 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.x (verified on 21.1.256,
ModDevGradle 2.x). Most of it applies to any 1.20.5+ GameTest setup.

## How

Run `gradlew runGameTestServer` with `@GameTestHolder(MODID)` + `@GameTest(template = "flat")`.
Tests share ONE world in a concurrent batch — neighbouring test structures sit only
~5–10 blocks apart, so anything with an 8+ block scan radius can see the next test's
entities/players.

## Gotchas

1. **Symptom.** Entity scans (`getNearestEntity`, goals) never see the test player;
   or they see it but the mob refuses to stay targeted.
   **Cause (two traps in one).** `helper.makeMockPlayer(...)` returns a bare `Player`
   that is never added to the level. `makeMockServerPlayerInLevel()` *is* added, but
   its anonymous `ServerPlayer` **hardcodes `isCreative() -> true`** — creative
   players are rejected by `EntitySelector.NO_CREATIVE_OR_SPECTATOR` and by
   `MeleeAttackGoal`: its `canContinueToUse` returns false for a creative or
   spectator player, and `stop()` then calls `setTarget(null)`.
   **Fix.** Build a real `ServerPlayer` yourself:
   `new ServerPlayer(server, level, cookie.gameProfile(), cookie.clientInformation())`,
   `new Connection(PacketFlow.SERVERBOUND)` wrapped in an `EmbeddedChannel`, then
   `playerList.placeNewPlayer(connection, player, cookie)`,
   `setGameMode(GameType.SURVIVAL)` and belt-and-braces `getAbilities().instabuild = false`
   etc.

2. **Symptom.** Spawned mobs suffocate, have no line of sight to anything, and
   `hasLineOfSight`/raycasts return `BLOCK` into stone.
   **Cause.** GameTest loads the structure one block above the reported
   `structureBlockPos` (the structure-block convention). A "flat" 5×5 floor NBT
   (25 blocks at local y=0) ends up with its *top surface* at local y=2, not 1.
   Entities spawned at local y=1 are pushed down into the gap under the floating
   floor or wedged inside it — eyes inside stone, zero LOS.
   **Fix.** Spawn entities and items at local **y=2** on a 1-block floor template.

entries.name: mcp__minecraft-modding__find-class
entries.description: Resolve a simple or qualified class name to fully-qualified class names within an artifact. Use this before get-class-source when you only have a simple name. Expert tool: prefer the entry tools (inspect-minecraft, analyze-symbol, compare-minecraft, analyze-mod, validate-project) first.

className.description: Simple name (e.g. Blocks) or fully-qualified name (e.g. net.minecraft.world.level.block.Blocks)

version.description: Explicit version; omit and set versionFromProject to resolve it from the workspace.

versionFromProject.description: Resolve the version from the project's gradle.properties / gradle cache (requires projectPath).

target.description: Same shape as resolve-artifact target (incl. {"kind":"dependency",...} to read a Fabric/loader dependency class like vanilla), plus {"kind":"artifact","artifactId":"..."} to reuse a resolved artifact. Object, not string.

projectPath.description: Workspace root for dependency or workspace target resolution.

entries.name: mcp__minecraft-modding__get-class-source
entries.description: Get Java source for a class. Default mode=metadata returns a symbol outline only; pass mode=snippet or mode=full to read source text. Not read-only: outputFile writes to disk. Expert tool: prefer the entry tools (inspect-minecraft, analyze-symbol, compare-minecraft, analyze-mod, validate-project) first.

mode.description: metadata = symbol outline only; snippet = source with default maxLines=200; full = entire source

version.description: Explicit version; omit and set versionFromProject to resolve it from the workspace.

versionFromProject.description: Resolve the version from the project's gradle.properties / gradle cache (requires projectPath).

target.description: Same shape as resolve-artifact target (incl. {"kind":"dependency",...} to read a Fabric/loader dependency class like vanilla), plus {"kind":"artifact","artifactId":"..."} to reuse a resolved artifact. Object, not string.

projectPath.description: Workspace root for Loom cache-assisted resolution

gradleUserHome.description: Gradle user home for Loom cache lookups (overrides GRADLE_USER_HOME).

scope.description: vanilla = Mojang client jar only; merged = merged runtime discovery; loader = loader-transformed runtime jars.

preferProjectVersion.description: Detect MC version from gradle.properties and override target.value

maxChars.description: Hard character limit on sourceText; truncates if exceeded

outputFile.description: Write source to this file path and return metadata-only response

detail.description: summary = terse (drops diagnostics/empties, slims candidates); standard = keeps fields, drops heavy diagnostics; full = everything.

include.description: Field groups to include regardless of detail, e.g. ["provenance"].

includeProvenance.description: Alias for include:["provenance"] (diagnostic metadata). Default false.

entries.name: mcp__minecraft-modding__resolve-workspace-symbol
entries.description: Resolve class/field/method names as seen at compile time for a workspace by reading Gradle Loom mapping settings. Expert tool: prefer the entry tools (inspect-minecraft, analyze-symbol, compare-minecraft, analyze-mod, validate-project) first.

descriptor.description: JVM descriptor. Empty strings are treated as omitted.

gradleUserHome.description: Gradle user home for Loom cache lookups (overrides GRADLE_USER_HOME).

detail.description: summary = terse (drops diagnostics/empties, slims candidates); standard = keeps fields, drops heavy diagnostics; full = everything.

include.description: Field groups to include regardless of detail, e.g. ["provenance"].
